Surat al-Fath (Chapter of Victory)

Its purpose is the meaning of its name, which encompasses the conquest of Makkah and what preceded it, namely the treaty of al-Hudaybiyah, the conquest of Khaybar and the like, and the fulfilment of the report about it, the victory of the Romans over the people of Persia. It also encompasses what branched off from the conquest of honoured Makkah: the conversion of the people of the Arabian Peninsula, the fighting against the people of apostasy (ridda), and the conquests of all the lands. All of this is gathered in the statement "that He may make it prevail over all religion." All of this is most manifest, as its beginning and middle speak of it in places, such as ﴿Certainly Allah fulfilled the vision of His Messenger with truth﴾ [48:27], to the end of the verse. Its conclusion is ﴿that He may make it prevail over all religion﴾ [48:28], and ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah﴾ [48:29], up to His saying ﴿that He may enrage the disbelievers by them﴾ [48:29], i.e., by the greatest conquest and what is less than it of conquests. ﴿Allah has promised those among them who believe and do righteous deeds forgiveness﴾ [48:29], as it was at its beginning for the Messenger (ﷺ), ﴿and a great reward﴾ [48:29]. Likewise with the rest of the conquests and what they contain of spoils, there is abundant reward for that in the abode of recompense. "In the name of Allah," the greatest King, who encompasses everything in power and knowledge. "The Most Gracious," who has encompassed the responsible ones with the blessing of promise and threat. "The Most Merciful," who has singled out the people of His party to establish His true religion, so He made them victorious over all the other servants.

* *

Since that was the surah of striving and this is the Surah of Victory, it is glad tidings (p. 274) to the strivers among the people of this religion of success, triumph and victory over every disbeliever. This is as will come from the placement of Surat al-Nasr after Surat al-Kafirun. The Surah of Fighting informed about the disbelievers, with the nullifying of their deeds, their destruction and annihilation by fighting, and the corruption of all their conditions. And it informed about those who believed in what was sent down upon Muhammad (ﷺ), with guidance and the setting right of their state. It concluded with exhortation to striving against them, after guaranteeing victory to whoever among them supports him, and the firmness of feet. It threatened whoever turns away with the substitution of others in his place, and that this substitute does not turn away from the enemy nor shrink from it. That was decisive for the lowliness of disbelief and the exaltedness of faith, and that very thing is the manifest victory. [He began this with his saying, as a conclusion to that, by his saying emphatically, informing that it is necessary and that] it is among what should be emphasized for the rejoicing of noble souls in it, and for refuting whoever has sickness in his heart, and they were the majority of people at that time.

﴿Indeed We﴾, i.e., by the greatness We have, which mountains cannot bear, ﴿have opened﴾, i.e., We brought about a conquest appropriate to Our greatness, for everyone attached to perfecting the causes that produce it, without doubt. For this reason it was expressed in the past tense.

Since the benefit of that accrues to him (ﷺ), because the elevation of the word of Allah occurs through it, He elevates him, and the earth is filled with his security, so none of them does a good deed except that he has its like of reward. Despite the shortness of their time, they will be two-thirds of the people of Paradise, and that will be an honour for him, along with other secrets which the disbelievers would be unable to grasp even the easiest of. He said ﴿for you﴾, i.e., by the treaty of al-Hudaybiyah in Dhu al-Qa'dah of the sixth year after the Hijrah, concerning which this surah was revealed, the two accompanying in the return from it to the honoured Madinah. Al-Azhari said: There was no conquest greater than the treaty of al-Hudaybiyah, because the polytheists mixed with the Muslims, heard their speech, and saw what was neither more just nor better. So Islam took hold of their hearts and took root in them, and within three years a great multitude embraced Islam. Likewise, part of the conquest was the strengthening of his command (ﷺ) by the confirmation of what was sent down to him in a surah about the Romans' defeat of the people of Persia, according to the narration of one who said it was at the time of al-Hudaybiyah. Then He increased it emphasis by saying ﴿a conquest﴾, and increased its magnitude by saying ﴿manifest﴾, i.e., with no ambiguity about it for anyone. Rather, every person of intellect knows by it that you are dominant over all the people of the earth, because you were alone, and the people of disbelief thought that you were in their hands, and that your affair would not go beyond your mouth. Then some weak people followed you, and they tortured them, and they were with them in the worst conditions. That was fixed in their minds for a lengthy duration of thirteen years. Then Allah rescued your followers from them, first by emigration to al-Najashi, may Allah have mercy on him, and second to the honoured Madinah, while they were reassured that you, and you are their head, no affair would be organized for them without you, and no remedy for their breaking would be achieved unless you were with them. They believed that you were in their grip, that there was no escape for you from them ever, nor any separation from their town. So Allah extracted you from among them, after He protected you against the normal course, while you were among them, from their killing you, despite their striving in that and their exhausting of their strength in harming you. Then they exerted their effort to prevent you from emigrating, but they did not succeed. Then [in] returning you, but they were unable, and they did not prevail nor triumph.

Rather, they were overcome and subdued. Then He supported you with righteous, good helpers, and you, despite your fewness, were like fierce lions and surging seas. Whatever direction you inclined toward, you overwhelmed it. You gained the upper hand over its people; you killed them or took them captive. You did not cease increasing and strengthening, while they diminished and weakened, until you came upon them in their lands, of which they were certain they were the kings, such that others could not overcome them there, nor even traverse it. They did not repel you from entering upon them except by mere compromise, and they asked you to lay down war for ease and reconciliation. The banners of conquest appeared in the fullest manifestation, and the people of hearts knew that you would necessarily be in mounting the heights and in your elevation to ranks of high matters (p. 277) and all kinds of affairs.

Imam Ahmad narrated from Majma' ibn Jariyah al-Ansari, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "We witnessed al-Hudaybiyah with the Prophet (ﷺ). When we turned away from it, behold, the people were shaking their camels. Some of them said: What is wrong with the people? They said: Revelation has come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: So we set out hurrying, and we found the Prophet (ﷺ) standing on his mount at [the side of] al-Ghamim. When the people gathered around him, he recited: ﴿Indeed We have given you a clear victory﴾ [48:1]. Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Is that a conquest, O Messenger of Allah? He said: 'Yes, by the One in whose hand my soul is.'"

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr said: The connection of this surah with the one before it is clear from several aspects, though some of them are obscure. Among them: Surat al-Qital commanded them to fight their enemy in His saying ﴿So when you meet those who disbelieve, strike the necks﴾ [47:4], and the verse. They were made aware of help upon the occurrence of truthfulness in His saying ﴿If you support Allah, He will support you﴾ [47:7]. This called forth the longing of souls for the state of the outcome, so they recognized it in this surah. So the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed We have given you a clear victory﴾, and the verses. Thus the Exalted acquainted His Prophet (ﷺ) with the magnitude of His favour to him, and followed that with glad tidings to the believers in general, saying: ﴿It is He who sent down tranquillity into the hearts of the believers﴾ [48:4], and the verses. It was joined to informing about the state of those who broke their pledge of allegiance to him, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the ruling concerning the Bedouins who stayed behind, and urging striving, and explaining the state of those with excuses, and the magnitude of His favour, glory be to Him, upon the people of His pledge: ﴿Certainly Allah was pleased with the believers﴾ [48:18]. He rewarded them with the conquest and the taking of spoils, and the glad tidings of the conquest of Makkah: ﴿You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque﴾ [48:27], up to what He, glory be to Him, mentioned of His great favour upon them, and reminded them in the Torah and the Gospel of what this noble surah contains.

Another aspect: when Allah, the Exalted, said at the end of Surat al-Qital: ﴿So do not weaken and call to peace while you are the superior, and Allah is with you, and He will not deprive you of your deeds﴾ [47:35], this was a summary of the magnitude of what He granted them and the grandeur of what He gave them. Surat Muhammad included the explanation and elaboration of this summary. This requires extended discussion, which you have not adopted in this commentary, and it is further understood from the previous indications in the first aspect.

Another, obscure aspect: His saying, the Exalted, ﴿And if you turn away, He will substitute a people other than you; then they will not be like you﴾ [47:38] is an indication of those who enter the religion of Islam from the Persians and others when the Arabs turn away. He also indicated this in His saying: ﴿O you who believe, whoever of you apostatizes from his religion, Allah will bring a people He loves and who love Him﴾ [5:54], and the verses. He, peace and blessings be upon him, indicated to that: "Woe to the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near. Today there has been opened from the barrier of Gog and Magog such as this," and he formed the index finger with the thumb. He, peace and blessings be upon him (p. 279), indicated the Arabs' turning away and the seizure by others, which is in the two verses. He only indicated, by his saying "today," to a reversal of order, and this matter was deferred to the days of Abu Ja'far al-Mansur. The Persians, the Kurds, the people of China and the China of China (which lies beyond Gog and Magog) prevailed, and that was a conquest, a might, and a manifestation of the word of Islam. These prevailed in plans and in the management of the amirate, and dominated others. For this reason he (ﷺ) made their coming a conquest, saying "opened today." Had he intended otherwise, he would not have used "opened." Do you not see Umar's saying to Hudhayfah, may Allah be pleased with both of them, in the hadith about the trials, when he said to him: "Between you and it is a closed door"? Umar said: Will that door be opened or broken? He said: Rather it will be broken. So there is a difference between opening and breaking, and he only indicated the killing of Umar, may Allah be pleased with him. Therefore he, peace be upon him, said "opened," and said "from the barrier of Gog and Magog," meaning from their direction, their side and their regions, because the Persians and those who came with them are the people of the directions adjoining the barrier. On this basis, His saying ﴿And if you turn away, He will substitute a people other than you﴾ [47:38] (p. 280) is an indication of the domination of those we have mentioned and their spread into the provinces, the religious districts and the scholarly positions. Since this was before its matter was clarified, it would give the impression of deficiency and error, so He explained that it is a renewal of conquest and an empowerment from Him, the Exalted, of the word of Islam. So the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed We have given you a clear victory﴾, and the verses.

Al-Qadi Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi mentioned, in Talkhis al-Talkhis, the scholars of the Malikis, indicating the variation of their ranks. Then he said: "The most resolute in inquiry and the strongest in it in determination are the people of Khurasan: non-Arabs in lineage and lands, Arabs in creed and faith, among whom the promise of the Truthful, the Confirmed, is fulfilled. Allah granted them the keys of verification when the Arabs turned away from the sciences and withdrew from them, and turned toward this world and secured themselves from it. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: O Messenger of Allah, who are these about whom Allah said: ﴿And if you turn away, He will substitute a people other than you; then they will not be like you﴾? He, peace be upon him, pointed to Salman and said: 'If faith were at the Pleiades, men from these would reach it.'" End of quotation.

(p-281) Having informed us of the conquest (al-fath) immediately after the surah beginning "Those who disbelieve," as a glad tiding of the ascendancy of the people of this religion and the defeat of the disbelievers, as will come in the pairing of Surah al-Nasr with Surah al-Kafirun, He therefore gave the reason for the conquest as forgiveness and what follows it. This is an allusion to the death of the Prophet (ﷺ), may my spirit be a ransom for him, my father and my mother, and a hint that what is intended by his removal to the abode of perishing is only the manifestation of the upright religion (al-din al-qayyim) and the annihilation of falsehood, so that his rank may be exalted and his elevation magnified. Thus, when the conquest occurs, the intended meaning is as the surah of al-Nasr, which was the one that pointed to the disbelievers, alluded to that, as is well known, recorded, and written. So the conquest, which is one of the three signs mentioned in Surah al-Nasr, over all the opponents, which is the greatest cause of the manifestation of his religion over all religion, which is the greatest sign of the nearness of his term (ajal), may my self be his ransom and the apple of my eye be shielded from all evil by him, is what He, exalted is He, mentioned, saying: ﴿That God may forgive you﴾. By shifting from the style of greatness in the first person plural (al-nun) to the style of the third person, which points to the utmost of majesty, by attributing it to the Greatest Name (al-ism al-a'zam, the Greatest Name of God), this indicates that this forgiveness is in accordance with the comprehensiveness of this Name, which encompasses all the Most Beautiful Names: ﴿of what preceded of your sin﴾, that is, the matter for which you were commanded to seek forgiveness during the fighting. This is among the things by which one moves from a perfect station to a station above it that is more perfect, so you see it as a sin in relation to the greater perfection of the second station. Likewise His saying: ﴿and what follows﴾. Al-Razi said: forgiveness, as considered, has degrees, just as sins have degrees: "The good deeds of the righteous are the sins of those brought near." End of quotation.

It is also permissible that what is intended is: that you may witness the forgiveness through the transfer to Us after knowledge of certainty (ilm al-yaqin), with the eye of certainty ('ayn al-yaqin) and the truth of certainty (haqq al-yaqin). The meaning is that God causes him (ﷺ) to pass away immediately after the conquest and the entry of all the Arabs, who will conquer all the lands and through whom God will guide all the rest of the servants in His religion, and Satan will despair of being worshipped in their peninsula except in insignificant ways, because the purpose has been realized: the cosmos is filled with his good deeds (ﷺ), and with the generality of what his name, mentioned in these two surahs, indicates, of praising God, exalted is He, in His perfection in His essence and attributes, through his followers reaching a limit that they will not be confined to afterward, and no created being will stand before them at any limit.

Since the completion of the blessing is realized through two things: the manifestation of the religion and the transfer to the companionship of the prophets, He, exalted is He, said, informing of the two things: ﴿and that He may complete His blessing upon you﴾, by transferring you from the world of witnessing to the world of the unseen, and from the world of generation and corruption to the world of permanence and righteousness, which is more specific to His presence and more deserving of His mercy, and by the manifestation of your companions after you over all the people of the religions, who will refute the doubts of Satan, crush every disbelief, raise the banners of faith in all the lands, after humiliating the people of aggression and erasing every tyranny.

Since their guidance is from his guidance, God, exalted is He, attributed it to Himself, informing him that it is a guidance befitting His noble side, as a delight to him, and so He said: ﴿and guide you﴾, that is, through the guidance of all your people, ﴿to a straight path﴾, that is, clear, majestic, manifest, leading to what is intended, from a Book in which there is no crookedness in any way, a guidance that requires adherence to it and steadfastness upon it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 48, verse 3:

﴿And Allah will help you﴾ with their help against the kings of the nations and their expulsion of all the multitudes, a victory whose attribution to His Name, which encompasses all greatness, is fitting. ﴿A mighty victory﴾, meaning: the one who is granted this victory overcomes everyone who opposes him, and nothing overcomes him, along with its permanence. Thus there is no humiliation after it, because the community that is granted victory by it is not overcome by anyone, and the religion which He decreed for its sake is not abrogated (naskh) by anything.

The commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 48, verse 4:

When the Prophet (ﷺ) had informed the believers through his dream that he would circumambulate the Sacred House (the Ka'bah), and he intended the lesser pilgrimage (ʿumrah) in the year of Hudaybiyyah, and the Prophet (ﷺ) set out, and there went out with him the elite of his Companions, one thousand five hundred, they were certain that they would perform the ʿumrah in that very journey. This conviction settled in their hearts and was absorbed by their hearts, so its removal from them became the most difficult thing imaginable. The polytheists confronted them after his she-camel had knelt down, and he (ﷺ) made a treaty with them that he would turn back from them in that year and perform the ʿumrah at the same time the following year. That, or even less than that, was shaking to belief and an invitation to the Satan of doubt regarding the religion. A similar situation occurred during the Isrā' (the Night Journey), when the Prophet (ﷺ) had not informed them of anything that would create confusion about his affair, and many people apostatized because of it. Almighty Allah said, indicating victory through the steadfastness of the believers in this distressing situation, to manifest the completeness of His power and the subtlety of His wisdom: ﴿He is the One﴾, that is, alone, ﴿who sent down the tranquility﴾, that is, firmness in the religion, ﴿into the hearts of the believers﴾, that is, those firmly established in faith, who are the people of Hudaybiyyah, after there had befallen them there what is of such a nature as to disturb souls and deviate hearts: the obstruction by the disbelievers and the return of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, without attaining their objective. None of them turned away from faith after the people had been agitated and shaken, even ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, despite being al-Fārūq and despite his description in the earlier Books as "a horn of iron." So what is to be thought of others regarding the splitting of their souls and the trembling of their hearts? And al-Ṣiddīq, may Allah be pleased with him, had such a firm footing and such an established root that it was known of him, may Allah be pleased with him, that he could not be outstripped. Then Allah made all of them steadfast. Al-Rāzī said: "Al-sakīnah (divine tranquility) is trust in the promise of Allah and patience with the decree of Allah. Rather, sakīnah here is specified as a combination of victory, strength, and spirit, by which the fearful find calm and the grieving find consolation. The effect of this sakīnah is dignity, humility, and the manifestation of resolve in affairs." End of quotation. Everyone who is firmly rooted in faith has a share in this verse, its fruit within easy reach.

When He had informed of what no one else could do, He gave the reason with His saying: ﴿that they might increase﴾, that is, in belief in the Messenger's statement when he said to them that they would certainly enter Makkah and circumambulate the Ancient House. Allah resolved for them, through this, the doubt by reminding them that he had not told them that they would enter in that year. ﴿In faith﴾ through this belief in the unseen, [that] their treaty with the disbelievers and their return [without] reaching their objective is in fact the very conquest, because the treaty is consequent upon it, and the spread of Islam is consequent upon the treaty, as existence later revealed, so that they might measure other commands by it, ﴿along with their faith﴾, which was established before this event. Al-Qushayrī, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "By the rising of the moons of certainty over the stars of knowledge-certainty, then by the rising of the sun of [true] certainty over the full moon of eye-certainty."

Since perhaps a wretched person might suppose something of power to be gradual in the taking of affairs, He said: ﴿And to Allah﴾, that is, the One who sent down the tranquility upon them, so that their victory in this ʿumrah would be in potential, and then soon it would be actual and present, that to Him alone belong ﴿the armies of the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, all of them, among them the tranquility. He directs them by His subtle workmanship and wondrous arrangement. Had He willed, He would have given the believers victory now in actuality, and destroyed their enemies with some of His armies or without any cause. But He did so so that the victory would be through you, so your affair would be exalted and your reward would be great, and the truthful would be distinguished in his victory from the liar. For the abode is the abode of trial, and building effects upon causes, in the generally prevailing manner, contains wisdom, not compulsion and the manifestation of the Word. So His hidden name is the apparent one in this abode, and therefore you see effects veiled by their causes, and none knows the realities except the perceptive. Do you not see that when this sūrah was revealed to him (ﷺ) and he recited it to them, some of the Companions, may Allah's good pleasure be upon them all, said: "O Messenger of Allah, is this a conquest?" Some of them said: "They have indeed barred us from the House and barred our offerings." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Evil is this statement! Rather, it is the greatest of conquests. Are you not content that you have come upon them in their lands, and they repel you from them with the arrow, and they ask you for the sanctuary, and they desire from you safety, when they have seen from you what they disliked, Allah has granted you victory over them, and returned you safe and rewarded? So it is the greatest of conquests. Have you forgotten the day of Uhud, when you ascended and did not turn toward anyone, while I was calling you from behind you? Have you forgotten the day of the Confederates, when they came upon you from above you and from below you, and when the eyes deviated and the hearts reached the throats, and you thought about Allah the thoughts?" Then the Muslims said: "Allah and His Messenger have spoken truly; it is the greatest of conquests. By Allah, O Prophet of Allah, we did not think about what you thought about; you are more knowing of Allah and His command than we are." And Allah revealed, as confirmation of the matter of the dream for those whose understanding of its reality was confused: ﴿Allah has certainly fulfilled for His Messenger the vision in truth: you will surely enter the Sacred Mosque﴾ [al-Fath: 27], the verse. So all these things, as you see, return to being hidden, with wonder, behind the veils of causes, and none perceives them except the masters of precise examination into the wisdom of Allah, glorified is He.

Since the foundation of all that has passed rests upon power through hidden matters, from which there appears weakness other than what time revealed of strength, and since the completeness of power depends upon the comprehensiveness of knowledge, Almighty Allah said: ﴿And Allah is ever﴾, that is, the Greatest King, eternally and everlastingly, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of essences and meanings, ﴿All-Wise﴾ in perfecting what He does. So He turned them back from this ʿumrah after He had arranged the matter of the treaty, so that people would be secure and mix with one another, because He knew that no one with sound intellect hears the Qur'an and sees what its people hold of firm adherence to it and of hatred for what they were in, of following the forefathers, without hastening to follow and entering the religion willingly. Glorified is He, He admitted Khuzāʿah into the Prophet's (ﷺ) treaty, and Banū Bakr, who were their enemies, into the treaty of Quraysh, so that they might transgress against them, and Quraysh would assist them, breaking the treaty, after the armies of Allah had multiplied and the supporter of the religion had grown mighty. Then Allah would open Makkah the honored through them, the banners of the religion would be unfurled, the flags of manifest victory would flutter, people would enter the religion in throngs, and the religion of Islam would prevail over all religions.

When he indicated the conquest through the victory and what accompanied it, and gave the reason for the faith through *sakina* (divine tranquility), he gave the reason of the proof, which is ﴿that they may increase in faith﴾ [al-Fath: 4]. He also gave the reason for what the King of the armies indicated, namely His management of them and His management of the cosmos for their sake, by His words, exalted is He, as an increase in the tranquility: ﴿that He may admit﴾, that is, by what He caused in the tranquility, ﴿the believing men and the believing women﴾ who were created with a disposition toward goodness, through the struggle of some of them and the entry of others into the religion through the struggle of (p-٢٨٨) the strivers. Had He empowered His armies against the disbelievers from the very beginning, destroying them or annihilating them without an intermediary, the entry of most of them into Paradise would have been lost; these are those who believed after the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyah. ﴿Gardens﴾, that is, orchards whose description does not reach your minds except by what you know through your minds, even though the matter is greater than that. ﴿Beneath which rivers flow﴾: the verb indicates, brings near, and partially specifies by His words ﴿beneath which rivers flow﴾. Wherever you wish to make a river flow from, you are able to do so, because water is close to the surface of the earth along with its firmness and beauty. Since water is not pleasant except when it is settled, He, exalted is He, said: ﴿therein abiding forever﴾, that is, without any end.

Since the hearer of this might suppose that His act of doing so was by merit, He said, as an indication that there is no cause except His mercy: ﴿and He will remove﴾, that is, He will cover with a thorough and comprehensive covering, ﴿from them their misdeeds﴾, which it is not wise for them to enter the Abode of Holiness, Paradise, before they are expiated, because of what they were involved in of them, of disbelief and other things. So that expiation was a cause for their entry into Paradise. ﴿And that is﴾, that is, this great matter of admission and the expiation that prepares for it. He placed the adverbial phrase first to magnify it, and so He, exalted is He, said: ﴿with Allah﴾, that is, the Greatest King, Possessor of majesty and honor, ﴿a great achievement﴾ (p-٢٨٩) that fills all directions.

Since the attainment of the greatest success includes the delight of the eye in taking vengeance on the enemy, and since the concealed enemy is more severe than the open, defiant enemy, He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿and that He may punish the hypocrite men﴾, meaning: He removes from them everything that makes them sweet (ʿudhūbah), ﴿and the hypocrite women﴾, because of what angered them of the increase in faith; ﴿and the polytheist men and the polytheist women﴾, because of their obstruction, which was the cause of the (shameful) position (al-maqām al-dahḍ), which was the cause of the sending down of tranquility (al-sakīnah), which was the cause of the strength of the people of Islam, through what resulted from it of the great number of those who entered it, which was the cause of the destruction of the people of disbelief, and after that, the punishment of the Fire.

When He had informed of their punishment, He followed it with a description of them, through what caused them to deserve it, and He said, may He be exalted: ﴿those who think evil thoughts about Allah﴾, meaning: the One who encompasses all attributes of perfection, ﴿the evil thought﴾, namely that He would not fulfill His promise to help His Messenger ﷺ and his followers, the believers, or that He would not resurrect them, or that He would not punish them for opposing His Messenger ﷺ and opposing his followers. When He, glorified and exalted, informed of their punishment, He explained it with His saying: ﴿upon them﴾, meaning: in this world and the Hereafter, through what Allah disgraces them with, from the multitude of His armies, their rage at them, and their subjugation by them. ﴿The circle of evil﴾, which they devised and plotted against the Muslims, from which they have no escape. So they are forsaken in every situation, a manifest forsaking that every person perceives, and an inward forsaking that is perceived by those among the possessors of insight whom Allah, may He be exalted, wills, as happened in this ʿUmrah. As for al-sūʾ (evil), with a fatḥah or a ḍammah: it is that which causes distress, like al-kurh (disliked), except that it has become predominant in being attributed to what is intended to be censured. The one with ḍammah follows the course of al-sharr (evil), which is the opposite of good. So said al-Zamakhsharī in al-Kashshāf.

Since the one upon whom the evil circles may not be one who is angry with, He said: ﴿and Allah became angry﴾, meaning: the Greatest King, with what He has of the attributes of majesty and beauty, so His anger prevailed ﴿against them﴾. This is an expression that He treats them as one who is angry, with what they have no capacity to bear. And since anger may not necessarily entail humiliation and distancing, He said: ﴿and cursed them﴾, meaning: He expelled them with an expulsion by which they sank to the lowest of the low, so they were removed from every good.

When He had established what is theirs in both abodes, and it might be thought that this applies only to the world and so does not necessitate the punishment of the Hereafter, He followed it with what pertains to the latter, and He said: ﴿and has prepared﴾, meaning: has now readied ﴿for them Jahannam﴾, which will meet them with scowling, rage, roaring, and frowning, just as they used to frown upon the servants of Allah, along with what it contains of punishment by heat, cold, burning, and other kinds of hardship. Since the implied sense is: "and it is evil as a destination (fa-sāʾat muʿaddan)," He joined to it His saying: ﴿and evil is it as a destination﴾.

Since this (passage) indicates that the disbelievers, despite the apparent multitude and the mutually supporting, abundant strength that is witnessed from them, have no weight, because affliction encompasses them in both abodes, and since that is a matter which necessarily produces a scattering of thought regarding what affects them in that way, (the verse) is joined to what is implied by its context, informing that the management (of affairs) on this basis is for wisdoms and interests that description falls short of, and as a repelling of what one whose faith is not firmly rooted might imagine, things from which God must be declared free: "And to God belongs the power entirely; He does what He wills with whom He wills, without any cause you see."

﴿And to God﴾, i.e., the Supreme King, ﴿belong the hosts of the heavens and the earth﴾, so He empowers whatever He wills of them over whomever He wills.

Since what was mentioned of the punishment of the enemies and the reward of the friends depends on perfect knowledge and utmost power by which retribution and might are exercised, He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And God is﴾ the King to whom no one has any command with Him, eternally and everlastingly, ﴿Mighty﴾, who overcomes and is not overcome, ﴿Wise﴾, who places each thing in its most fitting place, so that nothing attributed to Him, glorified and exalted is He, can be annulled.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 48, verse 8:

When it became clear that no one else has any part in bringing about victory, and the surah from its beginning was a setting of direct address and turning toward (the Prophet), no matter called for a summons with the particle of address (ya') or any other. It was as if it were said: "What is the benefit of the mission (risalah) to mankind?" It is answered by His saying, affirming what the surah was concluded with of the two attributes of might (ʿizzah) and wisdom (hikmah):

﴿Indeed We﴾ with what We have of might and wisdom ﴿have sent you﴾, that is, with what We have of greatness, which is the meaning of might (p-292) and wisdom, ﴿as a witness﴾ over their deeds, of disbelief and faith, obedience and disobedience: for those who were in your presence, by yourself; and for those who came after your death or were absent from you, by your Book, together with what We have strengthened you with of the guarding angels.

Since good tidings (bisharah) are beloved to souls, He encouraged them toward what He has of good things and made them beloved to them by forming the active participle from it for emphasis, so He, exalted is He, said: ﴿and a bringer of good tidings﴾, that is, to those who obey, with all kinds of glad tidings. And since warning (nidharah) is extremely disliked, none undertakes to deliver it except one whose knowledge of what it contains of benefits, which necessitates bearing the bitterness of undertaking to proclaim it, is complete, He brought it in the form of intensive emphasis, so He, exalted is He, said: ﴿and a warner﴾.

That which you may believe: those whom We have judged to be believers, from among those to whom We sent you. This is according to the recitation of Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr (reciting ﴿لِتُؤْمِنُوا﴾ with the third-person verb), while according to the others (who recite it with the second person) the meaning is: O Messenger, and whoever among his community We have decreed to be guided, renewing this at every moment and remaining steadfast in it; and likewise the actions after him. That is the greater gentleness, because in the intimacy of direct address there is hope of closeness. ﴿in Allah﴾, that is, the One to whom it is not proper for anyone among His creation (and all of it is His creation) to turn to another, since He alone possesses the attributes of majesty and generosity, ﴿and His Messenger﴾ (p-293) whom He sent, He to whom all things belong in both ownership and dominion, to all of His creation.

Since faith is an inward matter, it is not accepted by God except with evidence, and since faith in the Messenger is faith in the One who sent him, and faith in the Sender is faith in the Messenger, he made the pronoun singular and said: "and support him" (wa-yu'azzirūhu), that is, help him, strengthen him, and assist him against everyone who opposes him, and protect him from everyone who plots against him, exerting themselves in this by hand, tongue, sword, and other means, thus preferring him over themselves and others, in glorifying and magnifying him. This is the real sense of the root, and whatever departs from it is either of the category of removal, like 'azūr meaning a cuckold (dayyūth), or of the category of the first meaning, like blame and striking short of the legal punishment; for these require that the one blamed or struck avoid what was objected to in him, and thus he becomes great. So this is the use of the cause (malzūm) to denote the effect (lāzim), and it belongs to the vein of what has been said:

"My enemies have a favour and a benefit upon me, so may the Merciful never remove my enemies from me."

"They searched for my slips and I avoided them, and they competed with me and I acquired lofty things."

Since the meaning admits of removal as mentioned, he clarified the intended sense with His words "and honour him" (wa-yuwaqqirūhu), that is, strive to follow him well in exalting and revering him, by taking upon themselves all his burdens, so that tranquillity becomes necessary through the gathering of his concern and the greatness of his resolve, with the removal of what used to scatter his thought from every matter that troubles him. "And glorify Him" (wa-yusabbiḥūhu), that is, declare Him free from (p-294) every blemish, such as breaking the promise of entering Mecca and circumambulating the Sacred House and the like, and believe in Him absolute perfection. The three verbs may be understood as referring to Allah the Exalted, since whoever strives to subdue the disbelievers has done the act of one who supports and honours; thus the pronoun either returns to the one previously mentioned, or he made the two names one, indicating the unity of the two named in the matter. When their matter was one, he made the pronoun singular as an indication of that.

Since the love of Allah and His Messenger is accepted from them without limit, he said, speaking of that: ﴿morning and evening﴾, that is, in the evening and the morning, to join with it what lies between day and night.

[p. 295] When [the verse] mentioned the Messenger ﷺ and what he was sent with, and concluded the verse by stating that He is not pleased with remembrance of Him and His Messenger except through constant practice, either in action or in potential, while He used the singular pronoun to indicate the unity of will and love from the Messenger and the Sender, He clarified the intended meaning of the singular pronoun with His words, encouraging the following of him and warning his followers against even the slightest lapse or laxity in what they have entered into of faith, [p. 295] which is the purpose of the Message. He also mentioned [the other party] alongside him, in answer to one who asks: "What is the reason for using the singular pronoun when two are mentioned?" He emphasized this because of what has overcome human nature of being bound by illusion and of recoiling from what is unseen, with no guide to it except reason: ﴿Indeed, those who﴾.

Since the imperfect (mudari', the present tense) may be used to denote occurrence in general without a specific time limit, as I related at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah from Abu Hayyan and others, He used it to encourage the renewal of such [acts] and persistence in them, saying: ﴿pledge allegiance to you﴾, i.e., at the Pledge of al-Ridwan, and before it and after it, to what you have brought of the Message, whose greatest aim is warning, a warning based on opposition, which demands hardships, and whose pillars are steadfastness and patience. It is called "pledge" (mubaya'ah) because they pledged their souls in it to God for Paradise, and this is the meaning of Islam: whoever submits has sold himself to Him, glorified is He. [God says]: ﴿Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their souls﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:111], and so on.

﴿Indeed, they are only pledging allegiance to God﴾, i.e., to the Greatest King, because all your deeds, whether speech or action, belong to Him: ﴿and he does not speak from [his own] desire﴾ [al-Najm 53:3].

When He magnified their pledge by encouraging it in a way that implies warning, He increased its magnification with that in which the warning is more apparent than the first. So He said, clarifying the first: ﴿The hand of God﴾, i.e., [p. 296] the One clothed in greatness. Since He is exalted above what may be imagined of a bodily limb, which contains an aspect of deficiency, He indicated the negation of that by [the expression of] being above, together with what it implies of the magnification of the pledge. So He said: ﴿is above their hands﴾, i.e., in the pledge, exalted above them in power, might, subjugation, glory, and transcendence above every aspect of deficiency. For this reason He repeated the Greatest Name three times in this [verse], indicating a greatness beyond description and an exalted unseen beyond perception. Then He mentioned Him again by the pronoun, to signal pure unseenness. This is what is meant by magnifying the pledge and honoring the Messenger ﷺ, together with the definite knowledge of God's transcendence above every aspect of deficiency, whether indwelling or union, as is clear in the customs of the Arabs and very evident in their habits of discourse. No intelligent or ignorant person among them doubts it at all. So the curse of God be upon those who, out of obstinacy and with the innovation of union, take it literally, and upon those who follow them among the rabble and the vile, who opposed God and His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and all the great Imams and the rest of the people of Islam, and who were content for themselves to be followers of the accursed Pharaoh. And what a [dreadful] thing to be in manifest error.

When the speech of God Most High, though it takes the form of a condition and a threat, must necessarily have some occurrence of it, however small, and when the secret in expressing it with the present tense, "they pledge allegiance to you," is an indication of the breaking of the pledge of Qays ibn Jadd to Islam, [p. 297] for he hid in al-Hudaybiyah at the time of the pledge, at one moment, and did not pledge allegiance, [God] made this the cause and elaborated on it by way of encouragement and warning. So He said, expressing it in the past tense to signal that none of the people of this pledge would break it: ﴿So whoever breaks﴾, i.e., violates it at any time, making it like a worn-out cloak or a decayed rope that is unraveled ﴿breaks only﴾, and He expressed it in the present tense to indicate that whoever commits breaking is, at every moment, breaking anew ﴿against himself﴾, not against anyone else, for he is within sight and hearing of God, [who] is able over him and worthy of punishing him, after he has hastened upon himself the great disgrace in this world, and will be held accountable for his breaking with a painful punishment. This does not harm the Messenger of God ﷺ in any way, for God is surely his Helper. Likewise, anyone who is broken against, when God wishes to support him, His hand, glorified is He, is above every hand.

When He had completed the warning, because it is the place for urging fulfillment on which the establishment of the religion rests in the most eloquent manner, He followed it, as is His custom, with encouragement to complete the urging. So God Most High said: ﴿And whoever fulfills﴾, i.e., does the completing, the thorough and the extensive, ﴿what he has covenanted﴾. He placed the adverbial phrase first for emphasis, and said: ﴿with God﴾, i.e., the King encompassing every [p. 298] thing in power and knowledge, [fulfilling] this pledge and others, for his fulfilling is only for himself: ﴿He will give him﴾, i.e., by a promise that will not fail, ﴿a great reward﴾ whose description your minds cannot encompass. Whoever reads with the nun (we) makes manifest what was concealed in the Name [Allah] of the greatness of majesty. The verse is an instance of ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which one of two parallel elements is left implicit, the other being stated, and vice versa): He first mentioned that breaking the covenant is against Him, indicating that fulfilling it is for Him, and secondly the giving of the reward indicates the removal of punishment mentioned first. Its secret is that He clarified that what the breaker intends of harm to others falls only upon himself, because that is greater in deterrence from breaking, given that man is naturally averse to harm to himself and distant from it. He mentioned the reward for the one who fulfills because it is greater in encouragement.

The occasion of this Pledge of al-Ridwan was: "When the Prophet ﷺ understood from the kneeling of his she-camel at al-Hudaybiyah a sign from God, glorified and exalted is He, that He had not permitted them to enter the Sacred City on this journey, he went along with His will, glorified and exalted is He, since there was in it no opposition to what He had commanded, until the peace treaty was concluded, which was itself the conquest. In the course of that, he sent Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him, to Mecca the honored, to inform the Quraysh that the Prophet ﷺ had not come for fighting and that he wanted only to perform the minor pilgrimage. But rumors spread that he had been killed, so the Prophet ﷺ resolved to engage them in battle, and he took a pledge from the Companions [p. 299] may God be pleased with them, that they would not flee from him. Every one [who was] with him pledged, except Qays ibn Jadd, for he hid under the belly of his camel and did not pledge. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Every one of you is forgiven except the owner of the red camel."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 48, verse 11:

When the Exalted and Glorified One had mentioned the people of the Pledge of Pleasure (bay'at al-Ridwan) and attributed them to the presence of the Most Merciful (hadrat al-Rahman), the listener became eager for news about those who had stayed away from that gathering and lagged behind from the presence of that 'umrah. So the report about what they hypocritically do was resumed with His words, "﴿Will say﴾," that is, with a promise that admits no failure. He emphasized the matter of their hypocrisy, alerting to their audacity in it, their brazenness with it, and the gentleness of the Prophet (ﷺ), his intense mercy, [his kindness] and compassion, so He said: "﴿to you﴾," that is, because they know that you are the gentlest of creation in companionship and the greatest of them in compassion towards the servants of God. Thus they hope for your acceptance of their corrupt excuses in a way they would not hope from anyone else among the sincere believers. And they overlooked, because of the hardness of their hearts, that lying in your presence is in the extreme of ugliness, because you are the greatest of creation and the most perceptive of them, together with the news that comes to you from the Knower of the Unseen. He belittled their matter by depriving them of reason and making them objects of action rather than agents, indicating that they had been expelled from this station because they are base and vile wretches. So He said, may He be exalted: "﴿The ones left behind﴾," that is, those whom God left behind from you and did not find fit (p-300) for your companionship in this 'umrah, and He made them like a worthless thing that a person leaves behind, because there is no benefit in it, so it is not regarded nor valued. That was because when the Prophet (ﷺ) wished to perform the 'umrah, he called his companions, may God be pleased with them all, to it, and he called from among the Bedouins around the honored city those who had professed Islam. But God did not want their presence, because their Islam was not sincere, and had they come, the situation would have been corrupted by them. The preservation of God, by His power and strength, from corruption entailed another corruption, namely that it might be said: He only held back the enemies from them through their multitude, so they stayed behind because of the wisdoms God knew in their staying behind.

Since some sincere Ansar and others had stayed behind bodily while being present with him (ﷺ) in heart, He excluded them with His words: "﴿from the Bedouins﴾," that is, the people of the desert, lying and slandering, audacious against God and His Messenger. "﴿Our wealth and our families have occupied us﴾," that is, from answering you in this 'umrah. "﴿Our wealth and our families﴾," that is, because if we had left them they would have been lost, since there was no one among us to look after them, and you had forbidden the squandering of wealth and neglect of dependents. Then, as a consequence of this statement, whose purpose is evil, they said: "﴿So ask forgiveness﴾," that is, seek forgiveness, "﴿for us﴾," from God, if we have erred or fallen short.

Since this might deceive one who lacks insight, He refuted it with His words, alerting (p-301) that whoever is truthful with God is not occupied from Him by any occupier, and whoever is occupied from Him by anything, that is a misfortune for him: "﴿They say﴾." He used the present tense to indicate that this is their habit, from which they never desist. And since faith was afterward established, He did not express it by "the mouths," as He did regarding the hypocrites, but said: "﴿with their tongues﴾," that is, in the occupation and the seeking of forgiveness. He emphasized what the mention of the tongue implies, that it is an outward utterance, denying the true speech, which is the speech of the soul in every respect, with His words: "﴿what is not in their hearts﴾," because they had no occupation, nor did they have any intention in asking for forgiveness.

Since their action, this staying behind, their excuses, and their request for forgiveness, were done under the supposition that they thereby ward off that disliked outcome from themselves and obtain for themselves what they love, and it was as though it were said: "He knows their lying, so what shall be said to them?" the Exalted One began the answer with His words: "﴿Say﴾," that is, to these fools, admonishing them, its occurrence being a consequence of their deceiving One to whom no hidden thing is concealed, indicating that the intelligent person should find it ugly to undertake what carries a fear of its consequence: "﴿Then who can avail you﴾," O deceivers, "﴿from God﴾," that is, the King to whom no one has any command, because He has no equal, "﴿anything﴾" that would prevent you from Him, "﴿if He intends for you﴾," that is, specifically, "﴿harm﴾," that is, some kind of harm, great or small, so that He destroys the wealth and the families while you are careful in guarding them (p-302), so your presence will not benefit them, or He destroys you yourselves. "﴿Or if He intends for you benefit﴾" by preserving them through Him while you are absent, so your distance from them will not harm them, and He will preserve you in your own selves. The Exalted One's division of their condition into two categories, with the indefiniteness, is known: some of them will suffer harm, since among them are those who apostatized in the time of the apostasy (ridda), and some will receive benefit, since he remained upon Islam.

Since the decisive estimate is: no one can avail anything against Him, the Exalted, for them in that regard; rather He is capable of all that He wills. Your action, because of your coarseness, stupidity and density, is the action of one who supposes that He cannot prevail over you and does not know much of what you do, so that your lying is hidden from Him. But the matter is not as you supposed; He is not hidden from anything of your deeds. He built upon this what guided to its estimation, so the Exalted One said: "﴿Rather God is﴾," that is, the One encompassing always and eternally everything in power and knowledge, "﴿of what you do﴾," that is, the ignorant ones, "﴿Aware﴾," that is, He knows the inner aspects of these affairs of yours and others as He knows their outer aspects.

When he turned away from their assumption that their lying would be hidden from Him, by a general matter (which he mentioned first because it is more comprehensive in its benefit, given what it contains of inclusiveness), he followed that turning away with a turning away from the content of their speech, and said: ﴿Nay﴾, meaning: your staying behind was not due to the preoccupation with your families and property that you reported. ﴿You thought﴾, while you were standing with the apparent assumptions, having no access to the inner realities. He pointed to the firmness of their assumption according to their claim, and said: ﴿that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families﴾. Since the discussion concerned what is the state of the Messenger, namely setting out and travelling, [p. 303] he said, indicating that whoever sends a messenger to something he cannot defend, so that the messenger may carry that thing to the end he intended for it, is incapable of what he wants: ﴿the Messenger﴾. He also magnified the followers, saying ﴿and the believers﴾, using the description that is fitting for them and that conveys firmness. He made clear the confirmation of this in their view by the words of the Exalted: ﴿to their families, forever﴾, meaning: because of what was in your hearts of the greatness of the polytheists and the insignificance of the believers, which led you to say: "They are nothing but a mouthful for Quraysh."

Since a person may assume what is not obligatory, he said, indicating with the passive form that what their hearts contained, which must be declared far above Him, the Exalted and Glorified, being attributed to Him, though He is in reality the one who brings it about: ﴿And that was made attractive﴾, meaning: this evil matter, the ruin of the world, ﴿in your hearts﴾, until you loved it.

Since it was known that this was evil, he stated it explicitly in a way that encompasses others, saying: ﴿And you thought﴾, meaning: with that and with other things that follow from it, such as the manifestation of disbelief and what branches from it, ﴿an evil assumption﴾, meaning: one that left nothing of what is most hated without enveloping it. And when the whole of their matter was uncovered, he revealed its effect, saying: ﴿And you were﴾, meaning: in view of your gathering as a collective, in Our knowledge before that, by what We had created you upon, and by what the circumstances disclosed of it to whoever has insight, ﴿a people﴾ [p. 304] meaning, despite your strength in what you attempt, ﴿ruined﴾, meaning: in the utmost state of destruction, worthlessness, corruption, and absence of good, because you were created upon that corruption, so there is no separation for them from it. This is as it passed, with regard to the whole as a collective and not with regard to each individual, for many of them were afterwards sincere, and they remained steadfast and did not turn back.

Since the implied sense is: "That is because you did not believe. So whoever among you and others believes and is sincere, We permit him a garden and silk," He joined to it, in a general form, His saying: ﴿And whoever does not believe﴾ among you and others ﴿in Allah﴾ [i.e.,] the One who, in reality, has no existence apart from Him, ﴿and His Messenger﴾, i.e., the one He sent to make His religion prevail, and who is the one truly deserving of being attributed to Him, expressing him by the Greatest Name (ism a'zam, the supreme divine name). And for the sake of magnifying him [and belittling the one who hates him, and making his scheming seem feeble], He shifted to the mode of speaking with the form of majesty and said: ﴿then indeed We﴾, i.e., by the majesty that is Ours, ﴿have prepared﴾ for him or for them. This was the original form, but He said, attaching the ruling to the attribute, as a notice that whoever does not combine belief in both of them is a disbeliever, and that the blaze [is for one] whose disbelief is firmly rooted. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿for the disbelievers﴾, i.e., those who do not combine belief in the Sender and the Messenger, and so they are disbelievers by that, and they persist in the attribute of disbelief because they were created upon it, ﴿a blaze﴾, i.e., a fire of intense kindling and blazing. It is of great heat, causing madness, and the kindling of the inner being with hunger, such that its possessor is never satisfied, and the spreading of every evil. The indefiniteness here is for terror and magnification. This verse, together with what the context guided to conjoining to it, namely those who believe, indicates, although it is in the context of a condition, that most of them will make their faith sincere after that. (p-305)

When the account of the armies had ended, first in general and then in particular, of those who were called to march and the sincere ones, and He concluded with the punishment of the disbelievers, and since the one who disposes of the armies may sometimes be one of the king's close associates, so that his disposal over them is not complete, and since the king may not be able to punish whichever of his soldiers he wishes, and even when he is able, he may not be able to inflict every kind of punishment he wills, such as the blazing fire described and others, because his dominion is not all-encompassing, Exalted is He, linking to the verse about the armies, said: ﴿To Allah﴾, that is, the Supreme King alone, ﴿belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, the armies and others. He manages all of that as He wills; there is no repeller of His judgment and no one who can reverse it.

Since none of these had been punished with what the earlier nations were punished with, such as the wind and other things, He did not mention what lies between the two horizons. He mentioned the result of the exclusive possession of the dominion (p-٣٠٦) in the manner that the situation requires, of encouragement and warning: ﴿He forgives whom He wills﴾, that is, no one has any objection to Him in any way, ﴿and punishes whom He wills﴾, that is, because nothing is obligatory upon Him and nothing can compensate Him. He is not like the kings who cannot exercise such authority because of the abundance of equals who oppose them in general. From this unspecified division it is also understood [likewise] that among them are those who apostatize, whom He punishes, and among them are those who remain steadfast in Islam, whom He forgives, because He does not punish without a sin, although He has the right to do so, since He is not questioned about what He does and His dominion is complete, so His disposal over it is just in every case. And since whoever does something at one time may not continue to have the power over it, He said: ﴿And Allah is﴾, that is, the One encompassing all attributes of perfection, eternally and everlastingly, nothing has come newly into being for Him that did not exist before. Since He began the verse with forgiveness as an encouragement to repentance, He concluded with it, because the context calls for it. He added mercy as an honor to the Prophet of Mercy, by way of encouragement and as an indication that His mercy overcame His anger, and so He said: ﴿Forgiving﴾, that is, toward the sins of the wrongdoers, ﴿Merciful﴾, that is, bestowing honor after concealment in ways that minds cannot contain, and His power to bestow favor is like His power to exact retribution.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 48, verse 15:

When He censured those who stayed behind, by what He said of them, that is, the censure, namely that they are doomed after He had first stated that He had cursed them, and Allah (glorified is He) had promised the people of al-Hudaybiyah the conquest of Khaybar as compensation for them, for having prevented them from taking Makkah the honored, because of the profound and precise wisdoms He has in that, and He concluded by saying that His command is executed, and that this entails comprehensive knowledge, He indicated both of these matters by His saying, as a resumption, answering one who would seem to say: Will He forgive those who stayed behind, so that they become as if they had never stayed behind? ﴿They will say﴾, that is, by a promise that admits no breach.

Since the Prophet ﷺ was in a position where no one could hope to obtain anything from him contrary to the command of Allah, He dropped the form of address he had used when mentioning them at first, and said: ﴿Those who were left behind﴾, that is, to those among the Companions whom they hope will intercede for them to be allowed to march with his army ﷺ, because the ruling is hidden from him and the like. He did not restrict them to the Bedouins, so that it would include everyone else who used to stay behind. ﴿When you set out﴾ by Allah's enabling you ﴿to take spoils﴾

Since the wording implied taking, and the expression of the plural form of maximum plurality indicated its abundance, he stated the first explicitly, removing the metaphor, and said: ﴿to take them﴾, that is, from Khaybar. ﴿Let us follow you﴾, that is, in whatever state you wish of the base states. ﴿Let us follow you.﴾ Since allowing them to do that would necessitate breaking Allah's promise that it is specific to the people of al-Hudaybiyah, and that He had expelled the hypocrites and frustrated their intention, He (exalted is He) gave the reason for their statement by His saying: ﴿They wish﴾, that is, by your going with you, ﴿to change the words of Allah﴾, that is, the One who encompasses everything in power and knowledge, in announcing their curse and destruction, and that the conquest of Khaybar is specific to the people of al-Hudaybiyah, and that none shares it with them except those who agree with them in intention and emigration, so that they may thereby reach casting doubt upon the people of Islam concerning it. The meaning is that their action is the action of one who wants that. It is not far-fetched that they are of two kinds: some of them want that, and some of them did not want it but did the action of one who wants it.

Since the listener would be inclined to ask what is said to them, He said, addressing the most truthful of creation, upon him be blessings and peace: ﴿Say﴾, that is, O beloved, to them, when their speech reaches you, you yourself, for no one else can stand in your place in this important matter, in an emphatic statement: ﴿You will never follow us﴾, even if you strive for that. He framed it in the form of a negation, though the intended meaning is a prohibition, because it, while being more emphatic, is a sign of the signs of prophethood, and it is more restraining and more indicative of contempt.

Since this emphasis indicated that it comes from one whom nothing at all opposes in His intention, He explained it by His saying: ﴿Thus has Allah said﴾, that is, a statement of such a wondrous matter and exalted rank, ﴿before﴾ this time, and He is the One whose word cannot be broken, for He is not like kings who have no power to forgive whom they wish or punish whom they wish. He decreed that none attend Khaybar, whose spoils were intended, except those who attended al-Hudaybiyah, and commanded that. So what He said came after some of those who stayed behind strove to break it, for their greed changed them after they heard this word of Allah, so they asked to go out with him ﷺ, but they were prevented, and no one else attended it. That is because the Prophet ﷺ returned from al-Hudaybiyah in Dhu al-Hijjah of the sixth year, and remained until the middle of Muharram of the seventh year, then he went out with the people of al-Hudaybiyah to Khaybar, and Allah granted him its conquest, and he took all its wealth, both movable and immovable property. Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, his cousin, and some of those with him from the emigrants to Abyssinia came to him ﷺ while he was there after its conquest, and the Prophet ﷺ made them sharers with the people of al-Hudaybiyah, because they were not among those who stayed behind, but were late through the excuse of not having arrived in time.

Since they were hypocrites who believed none of these statements, but rather thought they were stratagems to reach worldly aims, He attributed to their saying that to him a warning of their boorishness and the corruption of their assumptions: ﴿They will say﴾, meaning, the matter is not as mentioned, of what he claimed to be the word of Allah, ﴿but﴾ it is only that ﴿you envy us﴾, so you do not wish any of the spoils to reach us. Since the implied meaning was: the matter is not as they claimed, He ordered upon it His saying: ﴿Rather, they were﴾, that is, by natural disposition and temperament, ﴿not understanding﴾, that is, not understanding with the understanding of the skilled and adept, ﴿except a little﴾ regarding the affairs of their worldly life, and among that is their affirmation of faith for its sake. As for the affairs of the Hereafter, they understand nothing of them.

(p-310) Since this would lead the hearer to ask whether this exclusion will continue, it is answered that they will be tested with a hard matter that God will bring about, to distinguish the sincere from others. So He says, repeating their description as one who stayed behind, to inform that in reality they did not stay behind, but were prevented, as an expulsion from them and a distancing that punishes them, because of what kept them from following the Prophet (ﷺ) on this 'umrah, namely fear of fighting the Quraysh because of their great might. This is like how He rewarded those who love him (ﷺ) with the opposite of what they had resolved upon, namely fighting until victory or death: He restrained their hands from them, and this became the cause of the greatest conquest and of being free to conquer Khaybar and take its many spoils without great hardship. ﴿Say﴾, O greatest of creation, ﴿to those who stayed behind﴾, and He increased their blame by attributing them to coarseness, so He says: ﴿of the Bedouins﴾, that is, the people of hard hearts. It is also possible that this qualifier is meant to exclude those who stayed behind from the people of Madina [so that it indicates that the Bedouins, at this call, divide into obedient and disobedient, as his division of them, glorified be He, indicates; and that those who stayed behind from the people of Madina] are, like the Bedouins in what caused them to make excuses, without hope of their reform. ﴿You will be called﴾ by a promise that admits no failure, by the report of One whose knowledge and power encompass all things, a comprehensive call and a general mobilization, because the attribution to all of them implies a caller whose leadership is valid (p-311), so obedience to him is obligatory. And He indicated their distance from their land by His saying, exalted be He: ﴿to a people﴾.

Since the expression implied that they have strength and might against what they attempt, He clarified the meaning by saying: ﴿possessing great might﴾, that is, severity in war and bravery together with cunning and shrewdness, ﴿mighty﴾. And since the meaning is as if it were said: "For what?", He, exalted be He, says: ﴿You will fight them﴾, that is, by the command of your imam, ﴿or they will submit﴾, that is, they will call you to them, so that one of the two manifest outcomes occurs, because the Word of God is the highest: fighting from you, or Islam from them. If they do not submit, there is fighting and nothing else; if they submit, there is no fighting, because the imam has no aim except raising the Word of God. Nothing other than these two matters can occur, such as allowing them to remain under the jizya (poll tax), or a settlement, or a truce for a period, and the like. This caller is Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, and the people are Banu Hanifa and others of the apostates (ahl al-ridda), to whom the call was made at the beginning of al-Siddiq's caliphate, may God be pleased with him. As for the view of one who said they are Thaqif, it is weak, because the call was not made to them; the primary aim was the conquest of Makka, and the matter of Hawazin, Thaqif and others was secondary to it in that expedition, and there was no dispute between them and him. Also, when the affair of Thaqif became difficult, the Prophet (ﷺ) left them until they later embraced Islam, and he also left the remnants of Hawazin, not pursuing them nor being commanded to pursue them. So the apparent meaning of the verse is that once fighting breaks out, it is not abandoned until Islam is attained. The view that they are Persia and Byzantium is also weak, since each of them (p-312) accepts the jizya from its people. Interpreting it as a merely linguistic submission with no reason to do so, when the literal meaning is possible, is also unfounded. The division indicated by the verse has in fact occurred: when they were called [to them, they divided] into an answerer, who were the majority, and God gave them the good reward in this world through spoils and fair remembrance, and that is what is hoped for in the Hereafter; and an apostate, who were few, and God made them taste the painful punishment in this world by being killed in the most shameful state, and He will make them taste the greatest retribution in the Hereafter. As for fighting non-Arabs, all obeyed in it, and the division indicated did not occur there. Thus it is established by this that they are the people of apostasy, and God is the Granter of success. For this reason, after the call to truth, He made the statement, repeating the speech about their condition and leaving it general, indicating that at the call they divide into one who turns toward it and one who turns away: ﴿If you obey﴾, that is, you carry out obedience to the one calling to that, who is Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, ﴿God will give you﴾, that is, He who has encompassing knowledge and power to give and withhold, and none can repel His command, ﴿a good reward﴾ in this world and the next. God made obedience to Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, in this matter specifically like obedience to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), whose obedience is obedience to God, as a reward for his particular steadfastness in submitting to what the Prophet (ﷺ) did of the treaty, and his firmness in responding as 'Umar, may God be pleased with them both, responded in the same way as the Prophet (ﷺ), without being present with him, as is known from the biography.

(p-313) Since opposing the Messenger (ﷺ) and whoever stands in his place can only come from a struggle against the primordial nature (fitra) and an effort to treat it, He expressed it with the reflexive form (tafa''ul), saying: ﴿But if you turn away﴾ from accepting his call, in disobedience, ﴿as you turned away﴾, that is, you treated yourselves and imposed upon them the turning away by staying behind from the Messenger (ﷺ), ﴿before﴾, that is, some earlier times that preceded this call, and that was at al-Hudaybiya, ﴿He will punish you﴾, that is, He will afflict you with a punishment that removes sweetness, in this world or in the Hereafter or both, ﴿with a painful punishment﴾ because of the repetition of that from you.

The Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on Surah 48, verse 17:

When he had threatened those who stayed behind for their staying away from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and then threatened those who held back from this imam who stands after him in truth, and since those with valid excuses could not easily do what this call demanded, and since the religion was founded on the easy, upright path (al-hanifiyyah al-samhah), he resumed with His words, the Exalted, calming what the threat had stirred in their fear: ﴿There is no blame on the blind man﴾, that is, for his staying behind from the call to go out with the Prophet (ﷺ) or with other leaders of the call. ﴿Is any blame﴾, that is, any inclination carrying the weight of sin, because his blindness weakens his effort and all his striking power. To reinforce the meaning, and to calm what had stirred in the fear of the believer, he repeated the negation and the blame in each separate clause, as an emphasis on this matter, and said: ﴿Nor on the lame man﴾, even though his deficiency is less than the deficiency of blindness, ﴿is any blame﴾. He made each clause independent as an emphasis on this ruling.

When he had mentioned these two particular conditions, for the greater harm they cause in the outcome when it comes to full jihad, he generalised with His words: ﴿Nor on the sick man﴾, that is, for any sickness, ﴿is any blame﴾. Thus the people of these excuses were not excluded, those whose excuses alone prevented them, from the people of al-Hudaybiyah. He left the blame negated unrestricted so that it would accept estimation of staying behind, and there was no need for that, since their presence is never free of benefit in jihad. It was stated in this way, without the form of exception, as a notice that they had not entered the threat at all, so that they would need to be excluded from it.

When he had given good news to those who obeyed that call, threatened those who sat back from it, and excused those who had valid excuses, and since answering the call was permissible for those with excuses, indeed better than their staying behind, for this reason He did not negate their answering; He only negated the blame. He spoke in a general form, joining by conjunction to what is implied, meaning: whoever among them stays behind, his staying behind is permissible for him: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah﴾, that is, the One encompassing all attributes of perfection, who pours out effects of His attributes upon whom He wills even if he is weak, and who withholds them from whom He wills even if he is strong, ﴿and His Messenger﴾, from among those with excuses and others, in whatever they have been urged to, whatever obedience it is, his answering is required, ﴿He will admit him﴾, that is, Allah, the Great King, as a reward for him, ﴿to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾. He drew attention to the nearness of attaining water by affirming the preposition in His words: ﴿beneath which rivers flow﴾, that is, wherever you wish, you make a river flow. ﴿And whoever turns away﴾, that is, whoever he is among those addressed now and others, from an obedience among the acts of obedience that were commanded, of whatever obedience it is, ﴿He will punish him﴾, that is, for his turning away, in both abodes or one of them, ﴿with a painful punishment﴾. The reading of the people of Madina and Syria, "We will admit him and We will punish him," with the nun, is more evident in indicating magnificence, for the sake of magnifying both the blessing and the retribution.

When He promised the obedient and threatened the disobedient, and souls incline more strongly toward promise, He indicated it with a great reward from Him, a tangible matter whose pull greatly affects souls that cannot penetrate the unseen world. He said, emphasizing it because the greatest intended audience of it were the wavering ones, and beginning with *qad* (indeed) because the context requires expectation, in accordance with the divine practice: when He stirs longing for something, He points to it with something witnessed that brings the promised unseen near: ﴿Indeed Allah was pleased﴾, that is, He to whom belong majesty and beauty, ﴿with the believers﴾, that is, those firmly rooted in faith. That is, He acted toward them as one who is content with what He had granted them of conquest and what He had decreed for them of reward. This also implies that He was not pleased with the disbelievers, so He forsook them in this world, along with what He prepared for them in the Hereafter. Thus these verses confirm, through matters that are witnessed, the recompense of the two groups mentioned.

When He mentioned the pleasure, He mentioned its time to indicate its cause, so He said: ﴿when﴾, that is, at the time when, and He described their condition to inform that it was joyful, pleasing, and very firmly rooted in contentment. He said: ﴿they pledged allegiance to you﴾ at the ʿUmrah of al-Ḥudaybiyyah, when the polytheists barred them from reaching the House. So you sent ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him, to them to inform them that you had not come for fighting but only for ʿUmrah. Then word reached you that they had killed him, so you called for the pledge (bayʿah) to fight them, and all who were with you pledged allegiance to you that they would not flee, so that you might fight the people with them. He increased the matter in clarity and restricted it, honoring the people of the pledge, by saying: ﴿under the tree﴾. The article *al-* here indicates a known, mentally identified reference. It was a tree at the place where the Prophet ﷺ was camped at al-Ḥudaybiyyah. Because of this pleasure it was called the Pledge of Ridwān (the Pledge of Good Pleasure). Al-Baghawī narrated, through the chain of al-Thaʿlabī, from Jābir, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "None of those who pledged allegiance under the tree will enter the Fire."

When He indicated their sincerity through what He described of them, He made the following statement a consequence of it: ﴿So He knew﴾, that is, by the comprehensiveness of His knowledge, ﴿what was in their hearts﴾, that is, their conformity to what they said with their tongues in the pledge, and that what occurred for some of them of agitation at accepting the truce and grief over it was only out of love for Allah and His Messenger ﷺ and preference for what he wills of raising His religion and making it manifest, not out of doubt in the religion. From this knowledge He made a consequence, encouraging the like of this newly arisen condition among them, by saying: ﴿so He sent down tranquillity (al-sakīnah)﴾, that is, the steadiness and calm of hearts in every state that pleases Allah and His Messenger. He indicated its greatness in that it overcomes fear, however great, by saying: ﴿upon them﴾. Thus it had the effect that they did not fear the outcome of fighting when they were called to it, even though they were, amid the multitude of disbelievers, like a white hair on a black ox. Nor did the truce affect them with the weakness and other signs of deficiency that appear in it, in their hearts at that dismal station and cramped situations, except for a short while until they saw the sincerity of the resolve of the Messenger ﷺ and his command proceeded in that matter with what he did and said.

When He, glorified and exalted be He, mentioned His favor upon them, which is the foundation upon which nothing is built except it, He followed it with its effects, so He said: ﴿and He rewarded them﴾, that is, He gave them a recompense for what He had bestowed upon them of obedience and tranquillity in it, a reward, turning toward them, filling the places of their need.
