He is worthy that a person should aim at Him and persist in seeking Him, because of His turning, His capacity, and His all-encompassing nature. ﴿with a conquest﴾, through the truce that Almighty Allah brought about, which resulted from making Quraysh unable to fight. ﴿near﴾, by the cessation of fighting, which after their ease, strength, and gathering required mixing of people with one another, so that whoever had been distant from the religion would enter it because of what he saw of its excellences. Therefore the greatest conquest will be the conquest of the noble city of Makkah, which is the cause of the conquest of all the lands.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 48, verse 19:

When He mentioned the conquest (al-fath), He mentioned some of its fruits, saying: ﴿And many spoils﴾. By using the form of the plural of maximum number (sigha muntaha al-juyub), He alerted that they are great; then He stated this explicitly in His saying: ﴿abundant﴾. And since a thing is sometimes applied to what is in potential rather than in actuality, He removed that possibility by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿which they will take﴾, and it is Khaybar. And since that was thought unlikely due to the multitude of the disbelievers and the fewness of the believers, He explained its cause, saying, coordinating it with what is implied in its context: by the might of Allah and His wisdom: ﴿And Allah has always been﴾, that is, the One having no equal, ﴿Almighty﴾, that is, He overcomes and is not overcome, ﴿All-Wise﴾, that is, He perfects what He wills, so it is not undone.

(p. 318) When that had been brought near, confirmed, clarified and established, He, glorified and exalted is He, turned to them with address, to make their hearing secure, and said, removing every possibility that could recur in the minds of those who stayed behind: ﴿Allah has promised you﴾, that is, the Great King, ﴿much spoil that you will take﴾, and He confirmed its meaning by His words ﴿much spoil that you will take﴾, that is, in what comes later from various lands which cannot be counted. Then He made the following a consequence of this promise, His words: ﴿So He has hastened this for you﴾, that is, from it, ﴿this﴾, that is, the treaty that He established between you and Quraysh, concerning the laying down of war for ten years and that you would come in the coming year, in this same month, as ʿumrah pilgrims. For this is the cause of all of that. Abu Hayyan attributed this to Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, and it is most evident. It is also possible that the meaning is: ﴿which He has brought about for you from Khaybar﴾, from its captives and its movable property and other things, ﴿and He restrained the hands of the people﴾, that is, of the people of Khaybar and their allies, the tribes of Asad and Ghatafan, from aiding the people of Khaybar or raiding your dependents, after they had intended to do so, after He had restrained the hands of Quraysh and those who entered into their covenant by the peace agreement, ﴿from you﴾, while you were in your state of fewness and weakness.

Since the intended meaning was: a mercy for you because of your obedience to Allah and His Messenger, and a reward for the piety of your hands, and so that you would see the near causes of the conquest through what enters people into your religion when they are addressed on account of faith, He followed this with His words: ﴿and that it may be a sign﴾, that is, these causes of conquest and submission to Islam, ﴿for the believers﴾, that is, among you, concerning your entry into the Sacred Mosque in safety during the ʿumrah, and then in the conquest; and among you and others, from those firmly rooted in faith until the Day of Resurrection, concerning all that Allah informs of, in accordance with what has been established as training in this arrangement which He has arranged for you, namely that He is Subtle (laṭīf), who brings great things about through the opposites of their causes as people see it. Therefore no believer should be alarmed by the multitude of opponents or the strength of those who rebel against him, ever. For the cause of Allah being with the servant is following (the Messenger) with excellence (iḥsān), whose pillar is steadfastness in faith, on which He hung the ruling. So wherever this is found, the hung-upon thing is found, which is victory, by means that are either clear or hidden. ﴿And guide you﴾ in a matter of this kind, which has come upon you and alarmed you, to steadfastness upon hearing the promise and the threat, and to confidence in their content, because He is Powerful and Wise, and so He does not break the appointment, by guiding you ﴿to a straight path﴾, that is, a broad, clear way leading to honour without any doubt. This is among the signs of prophethood. For none of those addressed by this verse, namely the people of al-Hudaybiyyah, deviated, and perhaps, Allah knows best, for this reason He did not say "and guide them" in the unrestricted form, as the context required, so that it would not include others who may appear sincere in faith and then deviate. For this reason most of the details of this sūrah are among the signs of prophethood, since they were reported before they occurred.

When Allah, glorified is He, gladdened them with the good news that the agreement would be a victory (fath) and that they would receive spoils of Khaybar, He followed that good news by indicating that they had no hope of acquiring or conquering it without His help. So He said: ﴿And another﴾, meaning: He promised you many other spoils besides these, and they are, Allah knows best, the spoils of Hawazin, after which nothing comparable had yet been obtained. Since Allah, glorified and exalted is He, knew that the Companions (ṣaḥābah), may Allah be pleased with them, would remain steadfast in it, except for anyone who would ordinarily be unable to defeat them and so seize the spoils, what was in His knowledge, exalted is He, was, because of its certainty, like what had already occurred and passed. He said, exalted is He: ﴿You were not able to obtain﴾, meaning: by what you knew of your own strength, ﴿over them﴾. Since the listener, after learning of their inability to obtain them, would expect information about the cause that leads to taking them, in a manner established for those who affirmed the promise of them, He began with the particle of expectation and said: ﴿Allah has already encompassed﴾, meaning: He who encompasses everything in knowledge and power, ﴿them﴾. Thus they were in the position of something encircled by a wall (sūrah), preventing any part of them from escaping your possession, or enabling anyone else to take any part of them. For this reason, and for generality, He concluded the verse with His words: ﴿And Allah is ever﴾, meaning: He who encompasses all attributes of perfection, eternally and everlastingly, ﴿over all things﴾, of them and of other than them, ﴿Competent﴾, possessing absolute power, because He is ﴿Knowing of all things﴾.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 48, verse 22:

When (Allah, glorified is He) had mentioned that He restrained the hands of people from you all, He mentioned their ruling had fighting taken place. Affirming His power, and linking it to something like: "So if He willed, He would have enabled you to perform the 'umrah," and emphasizing it in order to dismiss those among the Bedouins and others who consider that unlikely, (p-321) ﴿And if those who disbelieved fought against you﴾, that is, in this manner, ﴿those who disbelieved﴾, that is, those who made this description applicable among people in general, firmly rooted in it and those below them, namely the people of Makkah and those who joined them. They had gathered, assembled the Ahabish and those who obeyed them, and sent Khalid ibn al-Walid forward as their vanguard to Kura' al-Ghamim, and he had not yet embraced Islam. ﴿they would surely turn their backs﴾, that is, with the utmost of their effort, ﴿in flight﴾, routed.

And since their not being helped after turning away is also unlikely, given their abundant reinforcements and the strength of their zeal, He said, using a particle of distance: ﴿Then﴾, that is, after a long time and the multiplicity of helpers, ﴿they would not find﴾ at any time ﴿a protector﴾, that is, one who would act toward them with the care of a close friend, in compassion and protection, because of the great terror produced by that flight, ﴿nor a helper﴾.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 48, verse 23:

When this was a custom established long ago with the friends of Allah, the Exalted, wherever they were among the messengers and their followers, and [when it is the case that] Our host is the one that will prevail for them, Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿The way (sunnah) of Allah﴾, i.e., the One who encompasses this creation has established it in this time and what follows it, just as He has encompassed creation in the ancient age. For this reason He said: ﴿which has already passed﴾, i.e., a sunnah that is emphasized and does not change. He emphasized the prepositional phrase because [the statement that] fighting did not occur in the past time except after the revelation of the Torah. Thus He said: ﴿before﴾. As for before that, destruction only came about by a command from Allah without the hands of the believers. ﴿And you will not find﴾, O listener (p-322), ﴿in the way of Allah﴾ who does not break His word, because He encompasses all the attributes of perfection, ﴿any change﴾, i.e., any alteration from any changer who would change it into something in its place.

Al-Biqa'i, *Nazm al-Durar*, on Surah 48, verse 24:

Since it has been established that the disbelievers will be defeated even if they fight, and that this is among the extraordinary matters of custom, given their constant superiority in number and the scarcity of the believers, until God's command comes, this being a definitive proof that none but the One, the Subduer, the Capable, the Chooser, has ordered it, He joined to it another wonder: the fact that the people of Makkah did not change in this 'umrah for fighting, despite their covenant and pact to that effect, and despite their strength of resolve and their fierce obstinacy. So He said, joining it to what its meaning implies, this is He who established this general custom: ﴿And it is He who restrained﴾, that is, alone, without any helper in that, ﴿their hands﴾, that is, those who disbelieved among the people of Makkah and others, for all of them are one legal category, ﴿from you﴾, O believers, ﴿and your hands from them﴾.

Since the disbelievers, had they extended their hands, would have entered Makkah, given what God had decreed and established regarding the turning away of the disbelievers, He said: ﴿in the valley of Makkah﴾, that is, while each of you and of them is inside Makkah, you in actual condition and you in ultimate outcome. Al-Qaffal reported that he said: it is permissible that by it is meant al-Hudaybiyyah, for it is within the Haram. End of quotation.

He expressed it with the letter mim rather than the letter ba', as in Al 'Imran, to indicate that He did here what the meaning of this name required of gathering, cleansing, and purification. So He caused for them the means of gathering and of purification from sins, (p-323) through what the verse of the 'ma'arrah (the verse concerning the hidden believers) pointed to in the present, and through the verses of the conquest in the future. He fulfilled what its name indicates of "people" (ahl), contrary to analogy.

Since this was not encompassing all of the time to come, but He must extend the hands of the believers against them on the Day of Conquest, He introduced the preposition and said, exalted is He: ﴿after He had given you victory﴾, that is, He brought about your triumph over them with everything you sought from them, and made for you the advantage and might ﴿over them﴾. This is what the historians have related. They said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) summoned Khirash ibn Umayyah al-Khuza'i, may God be pleased with him, and sent him to the Quraysh in Makkah, and mounted him on his camel. Al-Taghallub said to him: Let him convey to their nobles what he came for. They hamstrung the camel of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and intended to kill him, but the Ahabish prevented them and let him go, until he came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ). The Quraysh sent forty or fifty men from among them and ordered them to circle around the army of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to catch someone of his companions for them. They were seized, and they were brought to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he pardoned them and released them. They had been throwing stones and arrows into his army. Then they mentioned his sending of Uthman, may God be pleased with him, to Makkah, then the Quraysh's sending of Suhayl ibn 'Amr for the peace treaty. (p-324)

Muslim related in his Sahih, on the authority of Salamah ibn al-Akwa', may God be pleased with him, who said: "When we made peace and mingled with one another, I came to a tree and lay down at its base. Four polytheists from the people of Makkah came to me and began to revile the Prophet (ﷺ), so I hated them. I moved to another tree, and they hung up their weapons and lay down. While they were like that, a caller called out from the bottom of the valley: O people of the Muhajirun, Ibn Zunaym has been killed! I drew my sword, then I rushed upon those four while they were sleeping, and I took their weapons and made them a bundle in my hand. Then I said: By Him who honored the face of Muhammad (ﷺ), none of you shall raise his head except that I strike the one whose eyes are in it. Then I brought them, driving them before me, to the Messenger of God (ﷺ). My uncle 'Amir, may God be pleased with him, came with a man from the 'Abalat called Mikraz, leading him to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) on a dry-bodied horse, along with seventy polytheists. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) looked at them and said: Leave them; let the beginning of the wickedness and its sequel be theirs. So he pardoned them, and God revealed (p-325) ﹘﻿﻿﻿ ﴿And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them﴾, the verse." End of quotation.

Muslim and al-Nasa'i related, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, may God be pleased with him, that eighty men from the people of Makkah descended upon the Messenger of God (ﷺ) from the direction of al-Tan'im, armed, desiring to catch the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions, may God be pleased with them, off guard (ghirrah). In al-Nasa'i's narration: They said: We will seize Muhammad (ﷺ) and his companions. The Prophet (ﷺ) took them alive, and spared them, so God, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿And it is He who restrained their hands from you﴾, the verse.

Since this and similar things, from the violence, harshness, sternness, and severity of the people of Makkah, and the gentleness and leniency of the Prophet (ﷺ) towards them, saddened most of the Companions, may God the Exalted be pleased with them, God the Exalted said, consoling them: ﴿And God is﴾, that is, the One encompassing in majesty and honor, ﴿of what you do﴾ — that is, what the disbelievers do, according to the reading of Abu 'Amr with the third person (ya'malun), and what you do, according to the reading of the rest with the second person (ta'malun) — ﴿at that time and what follows it, as it was before it, ﴾ ﴿Seeing﴾, that is, encompassing in knowledge of the inner realities of that just as He encompasses its outward aspects. So He causes it to occur in this abode, in which He has tied causes to their means, through the firmest of means, in your victory over them, your domination of them, and your subjugation of them. You will come to know what He has arranged of your entering the honored Makkah secure, fearing nothing, in the 'umrah of qada' by treaty, then in the conquest with a mighty host, whose tips of death's claws are fastened to the points of its spears, and the cups of death return submissively to its white blades, (p-326) so that most of the people of Makkah and others who are now strenuous against you will believe, and will become the dearest of people to you, preferring themselves in fighting the disbelievers over you. Then God will open the lands through you, and will make you prevail, and He, who is the greatest defender of you, will make you prevail over all of the servants.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 48, verse 25:

Since the preceding description of them applied in a way that includes all the disbelievers besides them, he specified them, explaining the cause of their being restrained from them, despite their deserving at that time destruction, punishment and ruin. So He said: ﴿They are﴾, that is, the people of Makkah and those who joined them, ﴿those who disbelieved﴾, that is, who went to extremes in this description with all their inner selves and the full extent of their outward conduct, ﴿and barred you﴾, in addition to their disbelief, in this umrah of al-Hudaybiyyah, ﴿from the Sacred Mosque﴾, that is, Makkah, the Sacred Mosque itself, and the Ka'bah, to disrupt what you were engaged in of the rites of ihram [for the umrah], ﴿and the offering﴾, that is, they also barred the offering you had sent to Makkah al-Mukarramah to be slaughtered there and distributed to the poor. Among these were forty camels, and in another report seventy camels (badanah), which the Prophet (ﷺ) had sent as an offering.

﴿Detained﴾, that is, in a state of being gathered and held back, along with your tending to it and tending to what it was offered for, ﴿from reaching its place of sacrifice﴾, that is, the place which is the most fitting of places for its slaughter, and which, when mentioned without qualification, the mind turns to. For the umrah this is al-Marwah. Slaughter is permitted in both hajj and umrah in any place within the Haram. So the place where the Prophet (ﷺ) slaughtered on this occasion, at the time of the ihsar (being prevented), was not its unrestricted place of sacrifice (mahall mutlaq).

Since the implied sense is: were it not for what he indicated of linking effects to their causes, He would have given you power over them, and you would have overcome them and taken the Mosque, and completed your umrah as you intended. Then he joined to this a more specific matter, saying: ﴿And were it not for men﴾, that is, residing among the disbelievers in Makkah, ﴿believing﴾ [that is, deeply rooted in faith, and therefore worthy of the description of manhood] ﴿and believing women﴾ [that is, likewise]. The excuse held back all of them from migration, because the disbelievers, given their numbers, oppressed them and prevented them from emigrating. Moreover, this includes whoever God had disposed toward goodness and whose faith He knew, even if at that time he was a polytheist. ﴿You did not know them﴾, that is, your knowledge did not encompass them from all aspects so that you could distinguish them by their persons from the polytheists, since they did not have the capacity to distinguish themselves at that time, and you did not know their locations so that you could deal with them according to what they deserved, especially in the state of war, spear-thrusting and striking. Then he substituted for "the men and the women" the phrase: ﴿that you trample them﴾, that is, harm them by killing or something close to it, such as wounds, beating, plundering and the like, of the kind of trampling which is the inflicting of war. From it is his saying (ﷺ): "The last trampling which God trampled was at Wajj." That harm would come from you to them, [assuming] they were polytheists, the harm of one who tramples upon what is trampled, and you would press upon them and seize them with a severe seizing, by force and dominance, such that you could not repel a hand that touched you nor be able to defend yourselves. ﴿Then there would befall you﴾, that is, as a consequence of this trampling there would befall you ﴿from them﴾, that is, from their side and by reason of them, ﴿a blame﴾, that is, a displeasing thing and a harm that is like war in its spread and its harm, and sin and betrayal through fighting without specific permission, and through not exercising thorough investigation, and a penalty, expiation, blood-money, regret, and reproach from those who lack knowledge. Then he attached to the trampling, which causes it, the befalling of blame, to complete the sense, saying: ﴿without knowledge﴾, that is, without knowing that they were among the believers.

Since the context indicates that the answer to "lawla" (were it not) is omitted, its estimate being: He would have given you power over them, and would not have restrained your hands from them. But He knew that, and He knew that some people among the polytheists would believe, so He bestowed favour upon you by lifting from you the burden of harming them without knowledge, and He arranged for you the causes of the conquest that was expected through giving you power over them, by an easy matter, and He restrained your hands and did not give you power over it. ﴿That Allah may admit﴾, that is, He who possesses all attributes of perfection, ﴿into His mercy﴾, that is, His honouring and bestowal of favour, ﴿whom He wills﴾, from among the polytheists, by inclining them toward Islam, and from among the believers, by rescuing them from them in the gentlest manner. When that was so, it produced His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Had they been separated﴾, that is, had they departed from one another, so that one of the two groups was removed from the other with a great removal, such that no category mixed with another, and thus the trampling of the believers upon them without knowledge would be secure, ﴿We would have punished﴾, that is, by your hands through Our giving you power, or by Our own power alone, without intermediary, ﴿those who disbelieved﴾, that is, who brought about the covering of faith.

Since this was general to all who were characterised by disbelief among the people of the earth, He stated explicitly what the context indicated, saying: ﴿among them﴾, that is, of the two groups, and they are those who barred, ﴿a painful punishment﴾, that is, intensely painful, by your hands or from Us, so that We bring you to your aim of performing umrah and prevailing over the disbelievers. Therein is an excuse and training in the good manners of some of them with others. And in the indication to the explanation of one of the secrets of God's withholding from them the power over them, there is an incitement for the servant not to accuse God in His decree, for perhaps He makes a matter difficult for him, which appears to him to be felicity, while within it there is a deadly poison. So God's withholding it from him is mercy inwardly, even if it is punishment outwardly. Therefore he must submit, while striving for goodness, eagerly seeking it, regretting its loss, and beware of objecting. Also in the verse, [that] God, exalted is He, may ward off from the disbeliever for the sake of the believer.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 48, verse 26:

When he had explained the condition for their deserving punishment, he explained its time, and in this there is an explanation of its cause. So he said: ﴿When﴾, that is, at the time when ﴿those who disbelieved set in their hearts﴾, that is, the hearts of their own selves, ﴿zealotry﴾, that is, (p-330) strong refusal, arrogance and disdain, which in its intense heat and its penetration is, among the hardest bodies, like poison and fire. Since this kind of zealotry may be a cause of mercy when it is for God, He said, explaining and magnifying its sin:

﴿the zealotry of ignorance﴾, whose basis is refusal in general, that is, whether it is with truth or with falsehood, so it prevents submission to the truth. Its foundation is the satisfaction of anger in accordance with what anger demands, for other than God, so it entails overstepping the limits of the Law. For this reason they refused that the Muslims should enter Makkah, the honoured, to visit the [Ancient] House, in which people are equal, and they refused to acknowledge the basmala. So this zealotry produced in them that they became arrogant toward the word of piety, lost their balance, and hastened toward polytheism, which is the most false of falsehoods.

Since this zealotry, together with its abundance, necessarily brings about the humiliation of whoever it is directed against, especially if he is few in number, He showed, as a sign that the matter follows His will and not the customary course, that it was affected by the opposite of what custom requires. So He said, as a consequence of this zealotry: ﴿Then God sent down﴾, that is, He who is not overcome by anything, and He overcomes everything, because of their zealotry, ﴿His tranquillity﴾, that is, the thing whose attribution to Him, glorified is He, is fitting: understanding from God and a spirit that produces tranquillity of the heart, which effects advancing against the enemy and victory over him, a sending down that was ﴿upon His Messenger﴾ (ﷺ), whose greatness derives from His greatness, (p-331) so he understood from God His purpose in this matter and acted in the most complete manner that pleases Him, ﴿and upon the believers﴾, may God be pleased with them, both groups in faith, because they are the followers of His Messenger (ﷺ) and the helpers of his religion. So He obligated them to accept his command, which [he understood from God and] which was hidden from most of them until [you understood it] (ﷺ) at the revelation of the surah of Muhammad, and He protected them from the whisperings of the devils. The zealotry that had entered the unbelievers did not enter them, so that they would fight out of anger for themselves and thereby transgress the limits of the Law. ﴿And He made them bind﴾, that is, the believers, an obligation of honour or dignity, not an obligation of humiliation and reproach, ﴿to the word of piety﴾, and it is every saying or action arising from piety and from exalting the word of sincerity, mentioned earlier in the surah of Fighting (Qital), and it is: there is no god but God, which is the truest of truths. It requires realising its meaning, that there is no doer but God, and steadfastness upon everything the Messenger of God (ﷺ) reported of monotheism, the basmala and prophethood, along with changing the writing of each of them for the sake of the unbelievers in that slippery position, where hardly any foot can stand firm. He attributed it to piety, which is taking a shield that protects from the heat of the Fire, and He made it a necessary attribute of theirs, not separated from them, because it is its cause and the thing that drives toward it. The impulse toward piety includes belief in oneness, which is: there is no god but God, for it is a word, as al-Razi said, whose beginning is the negation of association and whose end is attachment to divinity. This is one of the signs of prophethood, for the people of Hudaybiyyah who were obligated to this word all died (p-332) upon Islam. ﴿And they were﴾, that is, by nature and disposition.

Since among the unbelievers there were those who deserve it in God's knowledge and would become believers, He used the comparative form and said, exalted is He: ﴿more worthy of it﴾, that is, of the word of piety, than the unbelievers, the Bedouins and others of all creation. For this kind of generality He left the matter unrestricted by omitting the object of comparison. Since the one more worthy of a thing may not be its people from the beginning, He said, exalted is He: ﴿and its people﴾, that is, its guardians, those who keep to it with the closeness of a clan to its clansman, those who are bound to it and familiar with it. Since such a judgement can only come from one who knows, He said, connecting it to what is implied: since God knew the goodness of their hearts and their purity: ﴿And God was﴾, that is, the one who encompasses all existents in knowledge and power, ﴿of everything﴾, of that and of other things, ﴿All-Knowing﴾, that is, of encompassing knowledge, both subtle and manifest. The verse belongs to the rhetorical device of ihtibak (a figure in which two contrasting elements are mentioned and each is left implicit in the other): He mentioned the zealotry of ignorance first as evidence for its opposite second, and the word of piety second as evidence for its opposite first. Its secret is that He mentioned the gathering of evil first as a warning against it, and the gathering of good second as an encouragement toward it.

[p. 333] When God, glory be to Him and exalted, established His knowledge of the outcomes, because His knowledge encompasses all things, and He directed the causes by which He restrained the hands of both parties from each other, and He made clear what lies in that of benefits and what lies in the granting of power of harms, such as the killing of those among the polytheists who were judged to be believers, and the striking of those among the believers who are not known, and other matters, concluding with His encompassing knowledge, which entails the all-inclusiveness of His power, this produced His saying, for those who anticipated news about the dream, whose matter had disturbed them and whose mention had nearly shaken some of them, by way of emphasis: ﴿Truly﴾.

Since the dream has two considerations: one from the standpoint of its actual occurrence, which was unseen to the Companions, may God be pleased with them all; and the other from the standpoint of its report, which, together with the dream, is a witness with respect to Him, glory be to Him and exalted, He expressed it with truth and reality, saying, exalted is He: ﴿God has indeed proved true﴾, that is, the King who has no equal, who encompasses all the attributes of perfection, ﴿to His Messenger﴾ (ﷺ), who is the most honored of creation before Him, and who is independent of reporting what will not happen that it will happen; so how much more so when the one reporting is His Messenger. ﴿The dream﴾, which is part of revelation, because He, glory be to Him, sees the reality and knows its correspondence in that ﴿you will enter the Sacred Mosque in security, some shaving their heads and others cutting short [their hair]﴾, its report and the dream of His Messenger (ﷺ) being connected ﴿with truth﴾. This is because the content of a report, when it occurs and its details are matched between the reality and it, and the reality corresponds to it without any part of it departing from any part of it, the upshot is that if you attribute it to reality, it corresponds to it, and so it is truth; and if you attribute reality to it, it corresponds to it, and so it is real.

[p. 334] Since He swore an oath for the sake of emphasis to those who were being shaken, He answered them with His saying, emphasized by what conveys the oath as well, as an indication of the magnitude of the shaking: ﴿You will surely enter﴾, that is, after this, an entry whose matter has been decreed, ﴿the Mosque﴾, that is, the one around which the Ka'bah is circumambulated, and its entry is only by entering the Sacred Precinct, ﴿the Sacred﴾, that is, the one which God has made a refuge from the humiliation of tyrants and has prevented from every wrongdoer.

Since nothing is obligatory upon Him, glory be to Him and exalted, even if He has promised it, He indicated this by His saying, as a discipline for them, that some of them should say after this: "Did He not say that we would enter the House?" and similar things, and for others to say: "We will enter": ﴿if God wills﴾, that is, He who has the encompassing of the attributes of perfection, while you are ﴿in security﴾, not fearing [except] God, divided according to shaving and cutting short into two groups, ﴿shaving your heads﴾. Perhaps by using the intensive form he indicated that the doer of the truth is many; likewise ﴿and cutting short﴾, except that the placing first indicates that the first is more numerous.

Since entering in a state of security does not entail security after it, He, exalted is He, said: ﴿you will not fear﴾, that is, no fear will renew for you after that, until you enter upon them in the year of the conquest, prevailing over them by victory. Since it is known that the cause of this report is the encompassing of knowledge, the implication is: this is a matter of truth, which is to be trusted to the utmost [p. 335] trust, because it is the report of the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed; He, glory be to Him, has spoken truly in it, and He did not turn you back from it this time in this manner except for matters He arranged and affairs He made firm and decreed. He said, conjoining it to ﴿has proved true﴾, as a consequence of it or as a cause: ﴿so He knew﴾, that is, by means of a cause, or because He knew of the causes of the conquest, its impediments, and its being built upon wisdom, ﴿what you did not know﴾, that is, O allies, ﴿so He appointed﴾, that is, by means of the encompassing of His knowledge, ﴿besides﴾, that is, of the lowest rank of, ﴿that﴾, that is, the great entry in this year, ﴿a near victory﴾ by which He strengthens you, from the conquest of Khaybar and the laying down of war between the Arabs through this peace, and the mixing of some people with others as a result of that, which necessitates the conversion of many people by whom you are strengthened, so that that multitude and strength become the cause of the awe of the disbelievers which prevents them from fighting, so that killing becomes less, out of kindness toward the people of the sanctuary of God, the Exalted, in honor of this noble Prophet (ﷺ), from a raid and the striking of those among them of the Muslims who are weak without knowledge.

When he had informed of these great and subtle matters, which are founded upon the all-encompassing knowledge, He, glory be to Him, gave their reason and clarified their truthfulness with His words, exalted is He: ﴿He﴾, that is, He alone, ﴿is the One who sent His Messenger﴾, that is, the one of whom no messenger is more worthy to be attributed to Him (p-٣٣٦) (ﷺ) ﴿with guidance﴾, the perfect guidance which requires that most people be set upright by it. Had he informed of something that contained the slightest doubt, the sending would not have been with guidance. ﴿And the religion of truth﴾, that is, the matter which is firmly established and perfect in its firmness, to which reality corresponds. ﴿That He may make it prevail﴾, that is, His religion, ﴿over all religion﴾, the religion of the people of Makkah and the Arabs who worshipped idols. Its prevailing over it requires that he enter it safely, and its prevailing over others among the followers of false religions by the hands of his noble companions and those who follow them in goodness. It is a prevailing that is completed with the descent of ʿIsā, peace be upon him, together with gentleness toward creation and mercy toward them, so that none is killed except one who has no goodness whatsoever. And in proportion to tyranny, subjugation is achieved. Therefore, for this reason He manages His affair by means of such matters which necessitate His help and exalt His station, together with gentleness toward His people and fine dealing with His followers. So you will surely witness conquests of most of the lands and the subjugation of the harsh kings, by which you will recognize the power of Allah, glory be to Him and exalted is He.

When it was in the context of all-encompassing knowledge, and the implied meaning was: His Lord, glory be to Him, bore witness to his truthfulness in everything he said by manifesting miracles at his hands, He followed it with His words, exalted is He (p-٣٣٧): ﴿And sufficient is Allah﴾, that is, the One who possesses encompassing of all attributes of perfection, ﴿as a witness﴾, that is, the One who has sight and knowledge of the hidden essence of everything and its inner workings, for whom there is sufficiency in His affair. There is in reality no witness except Him, glory be to Him, because there is no encompassing, knowledge, or watchfulness except His, glory be to Him. He bears witness to everything His Messenger (ﷺ) informed of, specifically in this instance and generally in others.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 48, verse 29 (part 1 of 2):

When He (glory be to Him) concluded, with the all-encompassing knowledge of hidden and manifest things, the report about the Messengership, He specified it in His saying, in answer to one who says, "Who is the Messenger whose name is announced?": ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah﴾. That is, the King to whom none is equal, so he is the Messenger to whom no messenger is equal, for he is a Messenger to all creation, both those who reached his time in actuality in this world and those who preceded him potentially in it and actually in the Hereafter, on the Day when all are under his banner. The covenant was taken from all the Prophets that they would believe in him if they reached him, and those Prophets took this covenant from their peoples. The Mercy that encompasses everything is only prescribed for one whose knowledge of the All-Encompassing has occurred, that he believes in him. So no doer performs a righteous deed except that he has the like of its reward, whether that doer came before or after, whether he was from the people of the heaven or from the people of the earth. (p-338) This is a matter that none can count except Allah, the Glorified and Exalted. He indicated by this, with this name in particular, in the Surah of Muhammad, that he ﷺ is the Seal (al-Khatam), by what the letter mim indicated, whose place of articulation is the end of the places of articulation, and which encloses what its form indicates. It is repeated in the name after it for the utmost emphasis, and it is three (in the name Ahmad), as its name indicated: Ahmad. [This indicates] that, despite being the Seal, he is also the Opener (al-Fatih), by what his saying ﷺ indicated: "I was the first of them in creation and the last of them in being sent (ba'th)." The Surah of al-Saff was specified with him so as to balance this with the explicit statement of the one who gave the glad tidings, upon him be prayers and peace, concerning his coming after, in His saying: ﴿a messenger who comes after me, whose name is Ahmad﴾ [al-Saff: 6]. The mim at its beginning also indicated his being sent at forty. The remaining letters, which are ḥamd, indicate for him the perfection of praise in actuality in the fifty-second year of his life, which is the twelfth of his prophethood, with the pledge of the Ansar, may Allah be pleased with them. This Surah has indicated the words of sincerity (kalimat al-ikhlas) allusively, by what it mentioned of the word of Messengership explicitly; it concealed the majesty of Divinity and manifested the Muhammadan mercy. Just as it indicated the fighting (al-qital) allusively to the Messengership [and it explicitly stated the majesty of Divinity] by the words of sincerity, and what arises from fighting explicitly. A portion of the secrets of the two words was previously mentioned in the discussion of fighting.

When He mentioned the Messenger, He mentioned those to whom he was sent, saying, exalted is He: ﴿and those with him﴾, that is, with the companionship of his Companions and the good following of those who follow them with excellence. Since the honour of a people is an honour for their leader, He praised them with what encompasses him, saying, exalted is He: ﴿harsh against the disbelievers﴾, so mercy does not take them concerning them; rather, they are with them like a lion over its prey, because Allah commanded them to be severe toward them. ﴿Merciful among themselves﴾, like a father with a child, because Allah, exalted is He, commanded them to be gentle toward the believers, and there was no believer in their time except one who was of their religion, so he loves them and they love him, by the testimony of the verse of al-Ma'idah.

Since this was contrary to what the past nations were described with, that they did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of rebellion among themselves, it was a wonder, between the one who carries it by His saying: ﴿You see them﴾, that is, O observer of them, ﴿bowing and prostrating﴾, that is, constantly submissive; most of their times are prayer, in which the attribute of the angels has overcome their animal attributes, so the prayer was commanding them to good, purifying them from every deficiency and harm.

Since prayer is something into which showing off (riya') can enter, He made clear their sincerity with His saying: ﴿seeking﴾, that is, they seek by it and by other than it, in all their states, with their utmost effort and by making their intellects prevail over their desires and appetites, ﴿bounty﴾, that is, increase in good, ﴿from Allah﴾, that is, the One who has the encompassing of the attributes of perfection and beauty, who gave them the faculty of severity toward the disbelievers by what He bestowed of His majesty, and tenderness toward His friends by what He gave them of (p-340) His mercy, by which He prepared them to do good to His dependents. So they drew out desire from their breasts, and they came to see Him alone as their Lord, the one who does good to them, not seeing any lord other than Him, nor any doer of good besides Him. Since He mentioned their worship and their seeking increase in it and in other than it of the bounty of Allah, which cannot be reached in His worship except by His help, He followed it with the highest sought-after thing, saying: ﴿and good pleasure﴾, that is, a great pleasure from Him.

Since He mentioned the abundance of their worship and followed it with their sincerity in it, out of concern for it because it does not accept a deed without it, He indicated its abundance by His saying: ﴿Their mark﴾, that is, their sign which never leaves them, ﴿in their faces﴾. Then He clarified the sign by His saying: ﴿from the trace of prostration﴾. So it is a light on the Day of Resurrection, narrated by al-Tabarani from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ. This is in addition to what they have of the like of this in this world, from the trace of humility and awe, such that when one of them is seen, he causes the one who sees him to remember Allah, and when he recites, his recitation causes grief, humility, submissiveness and lowliness, even if his condition is shabby and his appearance poor. It should not be thought that among the marks is what some showy people do, making the appearance of a trace of prostration on the forehead; that is the mark of the Kharijites. In Ibn al-Athir's Nihayah, in the explanation of al-thafan: "And from it is the hadith of Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him: he saw a man with something between his eyes like the callus of a goat's knee, and said: 'If this were not there, it would be better' — meaning there was a trace of prostration on his forehead, and he only disliked it out of fear of showing off by it." And the author of al-Firdaws narrated from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Indeed I hate the man and dislike him when I see the trace of prostration between his eyes."

When He completed their description with this matter, which none can achieve except one whom Allah has purified from all his shares and desires, He indicated its loftiness, saying: ﴿That﴾, that is, this exalted description, very wondrous in its example, far in its attainment, ﴿is their likeness in the Torah﴾. Indeed it says in it: "Our Lord came from His place, and shone for us from Mount Se'ir, and appeared to us from Mount Paran, with ten thousands of holy ones at His right hand; He gave them and made them beloved to the peoples, and blessed all His holy ones, and they follow your traces." Its appearance from Paran is an explicit statement of the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ, for none came from it — and it is the mountains of Makkah by their agreement — after the descent of the Torah with prophethood other than him ﷺ. The "ten thousands of holy ones" is an indication of the multitude of his community, and that they are in purity like the angels; and their being among the people of the right hand supports this, as does their description as beloved to the peoples. All of this indicates what they are described with from us, from the testimony of existence. This is in addition to what I found in the Torah after their alteration of what they altered in it and their concealment, as Allah the Exalted said concerning many. The authors of the Conquests (Futuh al-Buldan) narrated concerning the conquest of Bayt al-Maqdis from Ka'b al-Ahbar that the cause of his conversion was that his father had told him that he had stored away for him two leaves (p-342), placed in a niche and sealed with clay over them, and commanded him to act upon them after his death. He said: "When he died, I opened them, and in them was: Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him, the Seal of the Prophets, there is no prophet after him; his birth is in Makkah, and his emigration is to Taybah; he is not harsh nor coarse, nor clamorous in the markets, nor does he repay evil with evil, but he repays evil with good, pardons, forgives and overlooks; and his community are the praisers who praise Allah for everything and in every state, and they glorify Allah with takbir on their tongues; Allah will give victory to their Prophet against everyone who opposes him; they wash their private parts with water, and they gird their middles; their Gospels are in their breasts; they eat their offerings in their bellies and are rewarded for them; their mutual mercy is like the mercy between mother and father; and they are the first of the nations to enter Paradise on the Day of Resurrection; they are the foremost, the near ones, the intercessors, and those for whom intercession is made."

Its origin is in the Sahih from Abdullah ibn Amr, may Allah be pleased with them both, and in al-Darimi from this Ka'b. For the authors of the Conquests, from Samurah ibn Hawshab, from Ka'b, who said: I said to Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, while he was in Syria at his departure: "O Commander of the Believers! It is written in the Book of Allah: 'Indeed this land in which the Children of Israel were, and they were its people, is opened to a man of the righteous, merciful to the believers, severe toward the disbelievers; his secret is like his public, and his public like his secret; his speech does not contradict his action; the near and the far are equal to him in truth; his followers are monks by night and lions by day, merciful to one another and generous to one another.'" Umar said: "May your mother be bereaved of you! Is this true?" I said: "Yes, by Him who sent down the Torah upon Moses, and who hears what we say! It is indeed true." Umar said: "Praise be to Allah who has honoured us, ennobled us, shown us generosity, and shown us mercy through Muhammad ﷺ and His mercy which encompasses everything." This is on the understanding that the intended meaning of "likeness" is description. It is possible that it is on its literal sense, and what is in the Torah is what I translated: "They are against their enemies like a horn of iron, and among themselves in benefit and connection like water and earth; for their Lord like the tender shoot of the crop with the wind and a sincere friend; and in turning to the Hereafter like the weary traveller and the weeping mourner." So he expressed it in our Book by what was mentioned.

When He mentioned their likeness in the first Book, He followed it with the second Book, which abrogates it, so that it may be known that he took from every Prophet who abrogates the law of his predecessor a covenant that he should describe them to his community, so that they would follow them when they call them. So He said: ﴿And their likeness in the Gospel﴾, that is, the one by which Allah abrogated some rulings of the Torah, ﴿is like a seed﴾, that is, like the likeness of a seed ﴿that sends forth its shoot﴾, that is, its offshoots, its leaves, and what emerges around its roots; all of that is its likeness.

When He mentioned this sending forth, He made the following a consequence of it, His saying: ﴿then it strengthens it﴾, that is, the shoot surrounds it, so it strengthens it and purifies it, without any sprout arising from it that would weaken it, and it equals it, faces it, and helps it. It appears that the reading with the hamza and the long vowel in the form of mufa'alah (fa'ala, "they help each other") is more eloquent than the reading of Ibn 'Amir with the short vowel, because when an action is between two parties pulling at it, the striving (p-344) in it is greater. Then He made the following of mutual support a consequence, His saying: ﴿so it becomes thick﴾, that is, the aforementioned seed and shoot sought thickness and brought it about, and so from it came its uprightness, ﴿so it stands firm﴾, that is, uprightness and justice were found in it to a great degree, as if it had been with the utmost striving and effort, ﴿upon its stalks﴾, that is, its stems, plural of sāq, which is that upon which a thing stands, while this aforementioned seed and shoot is ﴿pleasing the sowers﴾. It may also be that it is a resumed statement, expressing wonder at it, exaggerating its praise and showing joy in its affair. If it pleases them while they are in the utmost care for its affair, attentive to its condition, in contact with it, and knowing its meanings, it is even more pleasing to others. He gave the example because they are few and then multiply, with the splendour in the eye of the beholder, due to the radiance they have, whose source is the light of faith, the steadfastness of tranquillity and certainty, and the intense agreement of some of them with others, and the negation and removal of whoever opposes them. Examples were previously given in this book, at the end of al-Ma'idah, of parables struck in the Gospel with the seed; the closest of them to this is the parable of the mustard seed, so refer back to it.

Now when He (glory be to Him) had finished with their parable, He mentioned the fruit of making them as they are, saying: ﴿That He may enrage﴾, linking it to what is understood from the meaning of the discourse, namely that their being thus is for the purpose that He may enrage ﴿by them the disbelievers﴾, i.e., with a rage that is intense, of the utmost strength and firmness. This is because at the beginning of the matter they were few, and the disbelievers were hoping that their affair would not be completed; so whenever they increased in number as time went on, the disbelievers' rage at them grew. How much more so when they saw, together with their increase and strength, their beauty, freshness, splendour and radiance? Thus the rage is greater than it would have been had they been numerous at the beginning, because in that case it would have been repelled and its duration would have been short. Therefore, whoever hates a Companion is feared to be in danger of disbelief, because they are the first intended by the verse, while others are intended secondarily and by extension. And whoever hates all of them is a disbeliever. And if we take it as applying to others besides them, it is evidence that everyone who opposes the consensus (ijma') has disbelieved. So said al-Qushayri.

When their parable and the reason for their being thus were complete, He gave them good news, saying, in the place of promising them, and in order to link the promise to the attribute, following the custom of the Qur'an, as an encouragement to hold fast to it and a warning against turning away from it: ﴿Allah has promised﴾, i.e., the Supreme King, ﴿to those who believed﴾. Since the discourse concerns those who were with him (ﷺ), and companionship was evident in unity of religion, it was not inclusive of the hypocrites. So the concern to restrict it by "from them" was not present here as it was in Surat al-Nur; He therefore postponed it and placed the deeds first, because concern for it here is greater, since it is among their marks mentioned, so He said: ﴿and done﴾, i.e., confirming their claim to be with him in the religion, ﴿the righteous deeds﴾. Since His saying "with him" embraces, as has passed, those after the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them), and the deficiency among those after them was great, He restricted it by His saying: ﴿from among them﴾, i.e., from among those who are with him (ﷺ), whether they were of the original seed or its shoots which it brought forth, and they are the Followers (al-tabi'un) who follow them in goodness.

Since a human being, however diligent, falls short of reaching what is due to Him in worship, He indicated this by His saying: ﴿forgiveness﴾, i.e., for whatever lapses, or sins and misdeeds, occur from them, ﴿and a great reward﴾ after that covering. This concluding verse of this surah has gathered all the letters of the alphabet, as an allusive good news alongside the explicit good news it contains of the unity of their affair and the exaltation of their victory. That is because this 'umrah had brought them a breaking, in that they turned back before reaching their aim of entering the honoured Mecca and circumambulating the Ancient House, and that was not due to a fault that came from their side, as happened at the Battle of Uhud, as has passed in its explanation in Al 'Imran, which is the Surah of Tawhid, whose word is the word of piety (kalimat al-taqwa) at the second verse of this. So He (glory be to Him) gave them good news with what this surah contains of explicit good news, and with what this concluding verse contains of gathering all the letters of the alphabet, as an allusion that their affair must be completed, its course and fabric made firm and tightly bound, its arrangement and order made coherent, and its banners and standards raised high. He opened it with the mim of "Muhammad," which is dammah (vowelled with a damma), and closed it with the mim of "'aziman" (great), which is fathah (vowelled with a fatha), indicating, by what the mim has of closure in its place of articulation, that the completion of the matter has drawn very near, and its time has arrived; and by what is in its beginning of ḍamm (the damma) toward a lasting elevation in abundant praise, and by what is in its end of naṣb (the fatha) toward the completion of the conquest, its spread, its nearness and its renown, in a great manner and with honour in a mighty height. Its circularity also suggests that it is a matter with no end; rather, whenever it is concluded, it begins anew. It has become clear from this, and from what the explicit verse contains of the strength that empowers the believers and humbles the disbelievers, that its ending returns to its beginning: with the conquest for the Prophet (ﷺ), the great tranquillity for his Companions (may Allah be pleased with them), and mercy, forgiveness and the great triumph for all his followers, helpers and partisans (may Allah be pleased with them all). May He, by His grace and generosity, make us among them. This is the end of the first division of the Qur'an, which is the long (al-mutawwal). It has been concluded, as you see, with two surahs which in reality belong to the Prophet (ﷺ), and their essence is the conquest for him by the sword and victory over whoever fought him openly, just as the second division, the detailed (al-mufassal), was concluded with two surahs which are a support for him (ﷺ) by state over whoever intended him with harm inwardly. And Allah is the Guide to what is right, and to Him is the return and the final place. And may Allah bless our master Muhammad, his family and his companions.
